title: Dal Chawal
summary: Comforting arhar dal tempered with cumin, garlic, and ghee — served over steamed rice.
instructions:
1. Pressure cook dal with turmeric.
2. Temper with cumin, garlic, onion, tomato in ghee.
3. Pour over dal, serve with rice.

title: Aloo Gobi
summary: Dry potato and cauliflower curry with turmeric and cumin — a North Indian home favorite.
instructions:
1. Cut potato and cauliflower.
2. Heat mustard oil, add cumin, onion.
3. Add turmeric, coriander, chili.
4. Add potato, onion, tomato, cover, cook 15 min.

title: Chana Masala
summary: Spicy chickpea curry cooked with onion, tomato, and aromatic spices — rich in protein.
instructions:
1. Soak and cook chickpeas.
2. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic in oil.
3. Add tomato, spices, chickpeas.
4. Simmer 10 min, finish with garam masala and lemon.

title: Paneer Tikka
summary: Marinated paneer cubes grilled with bell peppers and onion — smoky and flavorful.
instructions:
1. Marinate paneer and onion, bell pepper in spiced curd.
2. Thread on skewers.
3. Grill or bake at 220°C for 12-15 min.
4. Serve with mint chutney.

title: Palak Paneer
summary: Creamy spinach curry with soft paneer cubes — nutritious and rich in iron.
instructions:
1. Blanch and blend spinach.
2. Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, tomato.
3. Add spinach paste, paneer, cream.
4. Simmer and serve with naan.

title: Rajma Chawal
summary: Hearty kidney bean curry cooked in thick tomato-onion gravy — a Sunday lunch essential.
instructions:
1. Soak and pressure cook rajma.
2. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic, add tomato.
3. Add rajma, simmer 15 min.
4. Serve over steamed rice.

title: Chole Bhature
summary: Spicy chickpea curry served with fluffy deep-fried bread — a beloved North Indian feast.
instructions:
1. Cook chickpeas, make chole gravy.
2. Knead maida dough with curd.
3. Roll and deep fry bhature.
4. Serve with pickle and onion.

title: Dahi Vada
summary: Soft lentil dumplings soaked in sweetened curd with tangy-spicy chutneys.
instructions:
1. Grind urad dal, fry vadas.
2. Soak in water, squeeze.
3. Pour sweetened curd over.
4. Top with chutneys and spices.

title: Butter Chicken
summary: Tender chicken in rich tomato-butter-cream gravy — India's most famous curry worldwide.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in curd and spices.
2. Grill or cook chicken.
3. Make gravy with butter, tomato puree, cream, spices.
4. Add chicken, simmer 10 min.

title: Aloo Paratha
summary: Stuffed flatbread with spiced mashed potato — the king of Indian breakfasts.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potatoes with spices.
2. Stuff into atta dough.
3. Roll and cook on tawa with ghee until golden.

title: Matar Paneer
summary: Green peas and paneer cubes in a spiced tomato-onion gravy.
instructions:
1. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic.
2. Add tomato puree, spices.
3. Add peas, paneer, cream.
4. Simmer and serve with roti.

title: Dal Makhani
summary: Slow-cooked black lentils in butter and cream — rich, velvety, and utterly luxurious.
instructions:
1. Soak and pressure cook urad dal and rajma.
2. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic, tomato.
3. Add dal, butter, cream, simmer on low 30 min.
4. Finish with garam masala.

title: Biryani
summary: Fragrant layered rice dish with spiced chicken, saffron, and aromatic herbs.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in curd and spices.
2. Par-boil rice with whole spices.
3. Layer chicken and rice, top with saffron milk.
4. Dum cook 25 min.

title: Masala Dosa
summary: Crispy fermented rice-lentil crepe filled with spiced potato masala.
instructions:
1. Ferment rice-dal batter overnight.
2. Make potato masala with mustard, curry leaves, onion.
3. Spread batter on hot tawa, fill with potato masala.
4. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Sambar
summary: Tangy lentil stew with mixed vegetables and tamarind — a South Indian staple.
instructions:
1. Cook arhar dal.
2. Boil onion, tomato, carrot with tamarind water.
3. Combine dal and onion, tomato, carrot.
4. Temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves.

title: Idli Sambar
summary: Soft steamed rice cakes served with lentil stew and coconut chutney.
instructions:
1. Ferment rice-dal batter overnight, steam in moulds for 12 min.
2. Prepare sambar.
3. Grind coconut chutney.
4. Serve together.

title: Coconut Rice
summary: Quick South Indian rice tossed with coconut, peanuts, and curry leaves.
instructions:
1. Cook rice and cool.
2. Temper mustard, urad dal, peanuts, curry leaves.
3. Add grated coconut, mix with rice.
4. Squeeze lemon, serve.

title: Upma
summary: Semolina porridge tempered with mustard, curry leaves, and vegetables — a quick breakfast.
instructions:
1. Dry roast semolina.
2. Temper mustard, curry leaves, peanuts.
3. Add onion, onion, carrot, peas, water.
4. Add semolina, cook until thick.

title: Pav Bhaji
summary: Mumbai's iconic spiced mashed vegetable curry served with buttered bread rolls.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potato, onion, tomato.
2. Sauté onion, tomato, ginger-garlic.
3. Mix in mashed potato, onion, tomato, butter, pav bhaji masala.
4. Toast pav in butter, serve.

title: Samosa
summary: Crispy deep-fried pastry filled with spiced potato and peas — India's favorite snack.
instructions:
1. Make maida dough with oil, rest 30 min.
2. Mash potato with peas and spices.
3. Shape cones, fill, seal.
4. Deep fry until golden.

title: Poha
summary: Flattened rice tossed with onion, potato, peanuts, and turmeric — a light breakfast.
instructions:
1. Wash and drain poha.
2. Temper mustard, curry leaves, peanuts.
3. Add onion, potato, turmeric.
4. Add poha, mix, squeeze lemon.

title: Egg Curry
summary: Boiled eggs simmered in a spicy onion-tomato gravy — protein-packed comfort food.
instructions:
1. Boil and halve eggs.
2. Sauté onion, ginger-garlic, tomato.
3. Add turmeric, cumin, chili, garam masala and water, simmer.
4. Add eggs, cook 5 min.

title: Chicken Curry
summary: Classic Indian chicken curry with rich onion-tomato-spice gravy.
instructions:
1. Sauté onion until golden.
2. Add ginger-garlic, tomato, spices.
3. Add chicken, cook 25 min.
4. Finish with garam masala.

title: Fish Fry
summary: Crispy pan-fried fish fillets marinated in turmeric, chili, and lemon.
instructions:
1. Marinate fish with turmeric, chili, salt, garlic, lemon.
2. Rest 15 min.
3. Shallow fry until crispy on both sides.

title: Lemon Rice
summary: Tangy turmeric rice with peanuts and curry leaves — quick South Indian lunch.
instructions:
1. Cook and cool rice.
2. Temper mustard, peanuts, curry leaves, chili.
3. Add turmeric, mix in rice and lemon juice.

title: Jeera Rice
summary: Fragrant basmati rice infused with cumin and ghee — perfect with any curry.
instructions:
1. Wash and soak rice.
2. Heat ghee, add cumin and bay leaf.
3. Add rice and water, cook until fluffy.

title: Gulab Jamun
summary: Soft milk-solid dumplings soaked in fragrant rose-cardamom sugar syrup.
instructions:
1. Mix milk powder, maida, ghee, baking soda into soft dough.
2. Shape small balls.
3. Deep fry on low heat until golden.
4. Soak in warm sugar syrup with cardamom and rose water.

title: Kheer
summary: Creamy rice pudding slow-cooked in milk with cardamom, saffron, and nuts.
instructions:
1. Boil milk, add washed rice.
2. Cook on low heat, stirring often, until thick.
3. Add sugar, cardamom, saffron.
4. Garnish with fried nuts and raisins.

title: Aloo Tikki
summary: Crispy spiced potato patties served with chutneys
instructions:
1. Prepare the filling/mixture with main ingredients and spices.
2. Shape into desired form (patties/balls/rolls).
3. Coat with breadcrumbs or batter if needed.
4. Heat oil for deep/shallow frying.
5. Fry until golden and crispy on all sides.
6. Drain on paper towels.
7. Serve hot with chutney.

title: Chole Kulche
summary: Spicy chickpea curry with soft leavened bread
instructions:
1. Wash and chop onion, tomato.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add cumin — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add onion, tomato, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until onion, tomato, peas are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Kadai Paneer
summary: Paneer in spicy bell pepper and tomato gravy
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the paneer. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add cumin, coriander, pepper, stir well.
6. Add paneer, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Paneer Do Pyaza
summary: Paneer with double onion gravy
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the paneer. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add cumin, garam masala, stir well.
6. Add paneer, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala, cream. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Methi Malai Murg
summary: Chicken in fenugreek cream sauce
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the chicken. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add garam masala, stir well.
6. Add chicken, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala, cream. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Paneer Bhurji
summary: Scrambled paneer with onion and spices
instructions:
1. Prepare paneer — clean, cut, and marinate with spices.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add paneer and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Kali Dal
summary: Slow-cooked whole black lentils
instructions:
1. Wash and soak urad dal for 30 min.
2. Pressure cook urad dal with turmeric and water until soft.
3. Heat oil/ghee for tempering.
4. Add mustard seeds, cumin, and curry leaves.
5. Add chopped onion, garlic, tomato — sauté until soft.
6. Pour the tempering into the cooked urad dal.
7. Simmer for 5-10 min, adjust salt and consistency.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Mixed Veg Curry
summary: Seasonal vegetables in tomato-onion gravy
instructions:

2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add turmeric, stir well.
6. Add potato, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Mushroom Masala
summary: Button mushrooms in spicy onion gravy
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the onion. Cut into even-sized pieces.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add cumin, garam masala, stir well.
6. Add mushroom, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.

6. Add brinjal, onion, tomato, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until onion, tomato, brinjal are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Bhindi Masala
summary: Okra stir-fried with onion and spices
instructions:

2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, stir well.
6. Add bhindi, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Gobi Manchurian
summary: Indo-Chinese crispy cauliflower in tangy sauce
instructions:
1. Cut cauliflower into pieces/florets.
2. Make a batter with cornflour, maida, and spices.
3. Coat cauliflower in batter, deep fry until crispy. Set aside.
4. In a wok, sauté garlic, ginger, and green chili.
5. Add soy sauce, chili sauce, and a splash of vinegar.
6. Toss in the fried cauliflower, stir-fry on high heat.
7. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot.

title: Veg Manchurian
summary: Mixed vegetable balls in soy-chili sauce
instructions:
1. Cut cabbage into pieces/florets.
2. Make a batter with cornflour, maida, and spices.
3. Coat cabbage in batter, deep fry until crispy. Set aside.
4. In a wok, sauté garlic, ginger, and green chili.
5. Add soy sauce, chili sauce, and a splash of vinegar.
6. Toss in the fried cabbage, stir-fry on high heat.
7. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot.

title: Paneer Lababdar
summary: Paneer in rich tomato-cashew gravy
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the paneer. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add garam masala, stir well.
6. Add paneer, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala, cream. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Dum Biryani
summary: Slow-cooked layered rice with marinated meat
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton with curd, spices, and salt for 30 min.
2. Wash and soak basmati rice for 20 min.
3. Par-boil rice with whole spices until 70% done, drain.
4. Cook mutton with sliced onions until half done.
5. Layer rice and the cooked mixture alternately.
6. Add saffron milk, fried onions, and mint on top.
7. Seal and dum cook on low heat for 25 min.
8. Gently mix and serve with raita.

title: Nihari
summary: Slow-cooked meat stew, Lucknowi specialty
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the beef. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add turmeric, garam masala, stir well.
6. Add beef, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

instructions:

3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.

6. Add chicken, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.

instructions:

2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add keema and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Chicken 65
summary: Spicy deep-fried chicken, South Indian bar snack
instructions:
1. Cut chicken into pieces/florets.
2. Make a batter with cornflour, maida, and spices.
3. Coat chicken in batter, deep fry until crispy. Set aside.
4. In a wok, sauté garlic, ginger, and green chili.
5. Add soy sauce, chili sauce, and a splash of vinegar.
6. Toss in the fried chicken, stir-fry on high heat.
7. Garnish with spring onions and serve hot.

title: Reshmi Kebab
summary: Silky smooth chicken kebabs
instructions:
1. Cut chicken into cubes.
2. Marinate with curd, spices, and lemon juice for 1 hour.
3. Thread onto skewers with onion and bell pepper.
4. Grill or bake at 220°C for 12-15 min, turning once.
5. Squeeze lemon and serve with mint chutney.

title: Medu Vada
summary: Crispy urad dal doughnuts, South Indian breakfast
instructions:
1. Wash and soak urad dal for 30 min.
2. Pressure cook urad dal with turmeric and water until soft.
3. Heat oil/ghee for tempering.
4. Add mustard seeds, cumin, and curry leaves.
5. Add chopped onion, garlic, tomato — sauté until soft.
6. Pour the tempering into the cooked urad dal.
7. Simmer for 5-10 min, adjust salt and consistency.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Rava Dosa
summary: Crispy semolina crepe with cumin and pepper
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal separately for 6 hours.
2. Grind to a smooth batter, ferment overnight.
3. Add salt to the fermented batter.
4. Heat a tawa/griddle, spread batter thinly in a circle.
5. Drizzle oil around the edges.
6. Cook until crispy and golden.
7. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Mysore Masala Dosa
summary: Dosa with red chutney and potato filling
instructions:

6. Add potato, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.

7. Simmer for 5-10 min, adjust salt and consistency.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Avial

instructions:

2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add curry leaves — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add drumstick, carrot, beans, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until carrot, beans, drumstick are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Rasam
summary: Tangy pepper-tamarind soup, South Indian comfort food
instructions:
1. Wash and chop tomato.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add cumin, mustard seeds, pepper, curry leaves — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add tomato, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until tomato are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Payasam
summary: South Indian milk and vermicelli pudding
instructions:
1. Boil milk in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring often.
2. Add the vermicelli and stir well.
3. Cook on low heat until thickened.
4. Add sugar, cardamom, and saffron.
5. Garnish with fried nuts and raisins.
6. Serve warm or chilled.

4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add fish and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

7. Cover and cook until potato, brinjal, drumstick are tender.

2. Rest the dough for 20 min.
3. Divide into small balls, roll into circles.
4. Deep fry in hot oil until puffed and golden.
5. Serve hot with curry or chutney.

title: Thukpa

2. Prepare filling with onion, carrot, cabbage/meat and spices.
3. Roll thin circles, place filling, fold and pleat edges.
4. Steam in a steamer for 12-15 min.
5. Serve with spicy red chutney.

title: Noodle Soup
summary: Clear broth with noodles and vegetables
instructions:
1. Wash and chop all vegetables (carrot, cabbage and onion) into small, uniform pieces for even cooking.
2. Heat a tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pot over medium heat.
3. Add finely chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and translucent.
4. Add the chopped vegetables and stir for 2-3 minutes to coat with the aromatics.
5. Pour in 4-5 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
6. Season with salt. Cover partially and simmer for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
7. For a creamy soup, blend partially with an immersion blender. For a chunky soup, leave as is.
8. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a drizzle of cream if desired.

instructions:

3. Add finely chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and translucent.
4. Add shrimp and cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned.
5. Add the chopped vegetables and stir for 2 minutes.
6. Pour in 4-5 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
7. Season with red chili and salt. Cover partially and simmer for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
8. For a creamy soup, blend partially with an immersion blender. For a chunky soup, leave as is.

2. If using fresh fruits or vegetables, wash thoroughly and chop into small pieces.
3. Add sattu and lemon to a blender or mixing glass.
4. Add water, milk, or ice as needed for your preferred consistency.
5. Blend until smooth (for shakes/smoothies) or stir well (for drinks).
6. Taste and adjust sweetness with sugar or honey. Add a pinch of salt to enhance flavor.
7. Strain through a fine sieve if you prefer a smooth texture.
8. Pour into serving glasses. Garnish with fresh mint, a slice of lemon, or crushed ice.
9. Serve immediately while fresh and chilled.

title: Kanji

1. Wash and prepare carrot. Cut into appropriate-sized pieces.
2. Heat oil or ghee in a suitable pan over medium heat.
3. Add aromatics — finely chopped onion, garlic, and ginger. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
4. Add mustard seeds and salt and stir for 30 seconds to bloom the flavors.
5. Add carrot and cook according to the method — stir occasionally to ensure even cooking.
6. Add water or stock as needed. Cover and cook until carrot is tender and fully cooked through.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and any finishing spices.
8. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and accompanied by rice, bread, or your preferred side.

title: Solkadhi

instructions:
1. Extract thick coconut milk from fresh or dried coconut.
2. Soak kokum in warm water for 15 minutes.
3. Blend coconut milk with green chili, garlic, and cumin.
4. Add kokum with its soaking water to the coconut mixture.
5. Season with salt and chopped coriander.
6. Chill in the refrigerator and serve cold as a digestive drink.

title: Kozhukattai

2. Boil water with oil and salt, add rice flour, and mix to form dough.
3. Knead the dough until smooth, divide into small balls.
4. Flatten each ball, place filling in the center, and seal into dumplings.
5. Steam the kozhukattai in a steamer for 10-12 minutes.
6. Serve warm drizzled with ghee.

title: Pitha

instructions:

2. Make the filling with grated coconut and jaggery.
3. Shape the dough into rounds, add filling, and fold into crescent shapes.
4. Seal the edges by pressing with a fork.
5. Steam for 12-15 minutes or deep fry until golden.
6. Serve warm as a traditional snack or dessert.

3. Season with salt and cumin.
4. For pita: mix flour, yeast, salt, and water into dough. Let rise 1 hour.
5. Roll into rounds and bake at 230°C for 5-7 minutes until puffed.
6. Serve hummus drizzled with olive oil and paprika alongside warm pita.

instructions:

2. Pound cold butter into a flat rectangle between parchment paper.
3. Encase butter in the dough and perform 3 letter folds, chilling between each.
4. Roll out and cut into triangles.
5. Roll each triangle from base to tip into crescent shapes. Proof 1.5 hours.
6. Brush with egg wash and bake at 200°C for 15-18 min until deeply golden.

title: Minestrone Soup
summary: Italian hearty vegetable and pasta soup
instructions:
1. Wash and chop all vegetables (tomato, beans and celery) into small, uniform pieces for even cooking.
2. Heat a tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pot over medium heat.
3. Add finely chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and translucent.
4. Add the chopped vegetables and stir for 2-3 minutes to coat with the aromatics.
5. Pour in 4-5 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
6. Season with salt and pepper. Cover partially and simmer for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
7. For a creamy soup, blend partially with an immersion blender. For a chunky soup, leave as is.
8. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a drizzle of cream if desired.

title: Quinoa Salad

instructions:
1. Wash and chop tomato.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add spices — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add tomato, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until tomato, peas, cucumber are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Ceviche
summary: Fresh raw fish cured in citrus juices
instructions:
1. Wash and chop onion, sweet potato, corn.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add chili — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add onion, sweet potato, corn, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until potato, onion, corn are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Chicken Shawarma
summary: Spiced middle eastern grilled chicken
instructions:
1. Prepare chicken — clean, cut, and marinate with spices.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add chicken and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Moussaka
summary: Mediterranean eggplant and meat bake
instructions:
1. Wash and chop eggplant, onion, potato.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add cinnamon — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add eggplant, onion, potato, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until potato, onion, eggplant are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Gelato
summary: Italian style creamy ice cream
instructions:
1. Heat milk and cream in a saucepan until just simmering.
2. Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale and thick.
3. Slowly pour the hot milk into the eggs while whisking (tempering).
4. Return to heat and cook until the custard coats the back of a spoon (82°C).
5. Strain, add vanilla or desired flavoring, and chill completely.
6. Churn in an ice cream maker until thick and creamy. Freeze for 2 hours before serving.

title: French Onion Soup
summary: Caramelized onions in broth with bread and cheese
instructions:
1. Wash and chop all vegetables (onion) into small, uniform pieces for even cooking.
2. Heat a tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pot over medium heat.
3. Add finely chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and translucent.
4. Add beef broth and cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned.
5. Add the chopped vegetables and stir for 2 minutes.
6. Pour in 4-5 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
7. Season with thyme. Cover partially and simmer for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
8. For a creamy soup, blend partially with an immersion blender. For a chunky soup, leave as is.
9. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a drizzle of cream if desired.

title: Miso Soup
summary: Japanese savory fermented soybean soup
instructions:
1. Wash and chop all vegetables (green onion) into small, uniform pieces for even cooking.
2. Heat a tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pot over medium heat.
3. Add finely chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and translucent.
4. Add tofu and cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned.
5. Add the chopped vegetables and stir for 2 minutes.
6. Pour in 4-5 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
7. Season with salt and pepper. Cover partially and simmer for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
8. For a creamy soup, blend partially with an immersion blender. For a chunky soup, leave as is.
9. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a drizzle of cream if desired.

title: Chili con Carne
summary: Mexican beef and bean spicy stew
instructions:
1. Wash and chop onion, tomato, bell pepper.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add cumin, chili, pepper — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add onion, tomato, bell pepper, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until onion, tomato, beans are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Enchiladas
summary: Tortillas filled and covered with sauce
instructions:
1. Prepare chicken — clean, cut, and marinate with spices.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add chicken and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Starfruit Salad
summary: Refreshing tropical fruit salad
instructions:
1. Wash and slice starfruit into thin star-shaped pieces.
2. Toss with mixed greens, cucumber slices, and red onion rings.
3. Add pomegranate seeds and toasted cashews for crunch.
4. Whisk together lime juice, honey, olive oil, and a pinch of salt for the dressing.
5. Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently.
6. Serve immediately as a refreshing appetizer or side.

title: Dragon Fruit Smoothie Bowl
summary: Bright pink breakfast bowl with toppings
instructions:
1. Freeze dragon fruit chunks for at least 4 hours.
2. Blend frozen dragon fruit with frozen banana and a splash of coconut milk until thick.
3. Pour the thick smoothie into a bowl.
4. Top with granola, sliced banana, chia seeds, and coconut flakes.
5. Add fresh berries and a drizzle of honey.
6. Serve immediately while still frozen and thick.

title: Fiddlehead Fern Stir-fry
summary: Rare seasonal forest greens
instructions:
1. Prepare the filling/mixture with main ingredients and spices.
2. Shape into desired form (patties/balls/rolls).
3. Coat with breadcrumbs or batter if needed.
4. Heat oil for deep/shallow frying.
5. Fry until golden and crispy on all sides.
6. Drain on paper towels.
7. Serve hot with chutney.

title: Truffle Pasta
summary: Rich pasta with aromatic truffle oil/shavings
instructions:
1. Cook fresh pasta (tagliatelle or fettuccine) in salted boiling water until al dente.
2. Melt butter in a pan over low heat.
3. Add a splash of pasta water and toss the drained pasta in the butter.
4. Season with salt and freshly cracked black pepper.
5. Generously shave fresh truffle over the pasta using a truffle slicer.
6. Finish with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and serve immediately.

title: Acai Berry Bowl
summary: Amazonian superfruit thick smoothie
instructions:
1. Blend frozen acai berry packets with frozen banana and a splash of almond milk.
2. Blend until thick and smooth — it should be thicker than a smoothie.
3. Pour into a bowl.
4. Top with sliced strawberries, blueberries, and banana.
5. Add granola, chia seeds, and coconut flakes.
6. Drizzle with honey or peanut butter. Serve immediately.

title: Persimmon Bread
summary: Sweet loaf made with seasonal persimmons
instructions:
1. Mix flour with salt, water, and oil. Knead into soft dough.
2. Rest for 20 min covered with a damp cloth.
3. Divide into balls, roll out into circles.
4. Cook on hot tawa until brown spots appear on both sides.
5. Apply ghee/butter and serve hot.

title: Durian Pastry
summary: Exotic and pungent fruit filling
instructions:
1. Remove durian flesh and mash until smooth.
2. Cook the durian flesh with sugar and coconut cream on low heat until thick paste forms.
3. Roll out puff pastry and cut into squares.
4. Place a spoonful of durian filling on each square.
5. Fold and seal the edges with a fork.
6. Brush with egg wash and bake at 190°C for 20-25 min until golden. Cool before serving.

title: Bison Steak
summary: Lean wild alternative to beef
instructions:
1. Gather all ingredients: bison ribeye, rosemary, garlic and butter.
2. If using fresh fruits or vegetables, wash thoroughly and chop into small pieces.
3. Add bison ribeye and rosemary to a blender or mixing glass.
4. Add water, milk, or ice as needed for your preferred consistency.
5. Blend until smooth (for shakes/smoothies) or stir well (for drinks).
6. Taste and adjust sweetness with sugar or honey. Add a pinch of salt to enhance flavor.
7. Strain through a fine sieve if you prefer a smooth texture.
8. Pour into serving glasses. Garnish with fresh mint, a slice of lemon, or crushed ice.
9. Serve immediately while fresh and chilled.

title: Ostrich Burger
summary: Very lean and high protein desert bird meat
instructions:
1. Mix ground ostrich meat with minced garlic, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and pepper.
2. Form into patties — handle gently as ostrich is lean.
3. Grill or pan-sear on high heat for 3-4 minutes per side (medium-rare recommended).
4. Toast burger buns on the grill.
5. Layer lettuce, tomato, caramelized onions, and cheese on the bun.
6. Add the patty and your favorite sauce. Serve with sweet potato fries.

title: Mangosteen Cooler
summary: Delicate tropical fruit infused drink
instructions:
1. Cut mangosteens in half and scoop out the white flesh segments.
2. Blend the flesh with coconut water and a squeeze of lime.
3. Strain through a fine sieve to remove any seeds.
4. Add honey or simple syrup to taste.
5. Pour over ice in tall glasses.
6. Garnish with mint leaves and a slice of lime. Serve chilled.

title: Uni Pasta
summary: Sea urchin creamy seafood pasta
instructions:
1. Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente.
2. Gently blend half the uni (sea urchin) with butter and a splash of pasta water.
3. Toss drained pasta in the uni butter sauce over low heat.
4. Season with a pinch of salt and white pepper.
5. Plate the pasta and top with remaining fresh uni pieces.
6. Finish with a squeeze of lemon and chopped chives. Serve immediately.

title: Escargot
summary: Snails cooked in garlic and parsley butter
instructions:
1. Clean and prepare escargot (or use canned, pre-cooked snails).
2. Make garlic-herb butter: mix softened butter with minced garlic, parsley, shallots, and salt.
3. Place one snail in each shell or escargot dish cavity.
4. Top generously with the garlic-herb butter.
5. Bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until butter is bubbling and fragrant.
6. Serve immediately with crusty French bread to soak up the butter.

title: Lion's Mane Steak
summary: Medicinal mushroom prepared like meat
instructions:
1. Gather all ingredients: lion's mane mushroom, soy sauce, garlic and thyme.
2. If using fresh fruits or vegetables, wash thoroughly and chop into small pieces.
3. Add lion's mane mushroom and soy sauce to a blender or mixing glass.
4. Add water, milk, or ice as needed for your preferred consistency.
5. Blend until smooth (for shakes/smoothies) or stir well (for drinks).
6. Taste and adjust sweetness with sugar or honey. Add a pinch of salt to enhance flavor.
7. Strain through a fine sieve if you prefer a smooth texture.
8. Pour into serving glasses. Garnish with fresh mint, a slice of lemon, or crushed ice.
9. Serve immediately while fresh and chilled.

title: Goat Cheese Stuffed Fig
summary: Sweet figs with tangy artisanal cheese
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 190°C.
2. Cut fresh figs in half and press a small well into each center.
3. Fill each fig half with a spoonful of soft goat cheese.
4. Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.
5. Bake for 10-12 minutes until figs are soft and cheese is warm.
6. Finish with a drizzle of balsamic glaze and fresh thyme. Serve warm.

title: Artichoke Heart Confit
summary: Slow-cooked edible flower hearts
instructions:
1. Trim and clean artichoke hearts, removing tough outer leaves.
2. Place artichoke hearts in a deep pan and cover with olive oil.
3. Add garlic cloves, lemon slices, thyme, and bay leaves.
4. Cook on very low heat (below simmering) for 45-60 minutes until tender.
5. Let the artichokes cool in the oil.
6. Serve at room temperature with crusty bread, or use in salads and pasta.

title: Bird's Nest Soup
summary: Delicately sweet edible nest dessert
instructions:
1. Wash and chop all vegetables (mixed vegetables) into small, uniform pieces for even cooking.
2. Heat a tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pot over medium heat.
3. Add finely chopped onion and garlic. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and translucent.
4. Add the chopped vegetables and stir for 2-3 minutes to coat with the aromatics.
5. Pour in 4-5 cups of water or stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
6. Season with salt and pepper. Cover partially and simmer for 15-20 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
7. For a creamy soup, blend partially with an immersion blender. For a chunky soup, leave as is.
8. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and a drizzle of cream if desired.

title: Rambutan Curry
summary: Sweet and savory tropical fruit curry
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the tofu. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add basil, stir well.
6. Add tofu, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Kangaroo Skewers
summary: Lean game meat from Australia
instructions:
1. Cut kangaroo meat into cubes and marinate with olive oil, garlic, rosemary, and lemon juice for 2 hours.
2. Thread marinated meat onto skewers alternating with bell pepper and onion.
3. Preheat grill to high heat.
4. Grill skewers 2-3 minutes per side — kangaroo is best medium-rare.
5. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
6. Serve with a native pepper berry sauce or chimichurri.

title: Bisibelebath
summary: Spiced lentil rice from Karnataka
instructions:
1. Cook rice and spread to cool.
2. Heat oil/ghee for tempering.
3. Add mustard seeds, urad dal, peanuts, curry leaves.
4. Add any carrot, beans and sauté briefly.
5. Add the flavoring (lemon/tamarind/spice paste).
6. Toss in the cooked rice, mix gently.
7. Adjust salt and serve.

title: Thoriyan
summary: Kerala style dry vegetable stir-fry
instructions:
1. Cook toor dal until soft and mash well.
2. Chop vegetables (ash gourd, raw banana, or yam) into small pieces and boil until tender.
3. Mix cooked dal with vegetables, grated coconut, and ground cumin.
4. Season with salt and a pinch of turmeric.
5. Temper with coconut oil, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and dried red chili.
6. Serve as a side dish with rice.

title: Alleppey Fish Curry
summary: Tangy mango and coconut fish curry
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the fish. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add turmeric, curry leaves, stir well.
6. Add fish, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Pori Urundai
summary: Sweet puffed rice balls with jaggery
instructions:
1. Heat jaggery with a little water until it melts and reaches one-string consistency.
2. Add cardamom powder and a pinch of dry ginger powder.
3. Pour the jaggery syrup over puffed rice (pori) in a large bowl.
4. Mix quickly and thoroughly while the syrup is still warm.
5. Grease your palms with ghee and shape into tight round balls.
6. Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

title: Murukku
summary: Crunchy rice flour savory snack
instructions:
1. Wash and soak urad dal flour for 30 min.
2. Pressure cook urad dal flour with turmeric and water until soft.
3. Heat oil/ghee for tempering.
4. Add mustard seeds, cumin, and curry leaves.
5. Add chopped onion, garlic, tomato — sauté until soft.
6. Pour the tempering into the cooked urad dal flour.
7. Simmer for 5-10 min, adjust salt and consistency.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Achappam
summary: Rose shaped crunchy fried cookie
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal separately for 6 hours.
2. Grind to a smooth batter, ferment overnight.
3. Add salt to the fermented batter.
4. Heat a tawa/griddle, spread batter thinly in a circle.
5. Drizzle oil around the edges.
6. Cook until crispy and golden.
7. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Unniyappam
summary: Sweet fried rice and banana balls
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal separately for 6 hours.
2. Grind to a smooth batter, ferment overnight.
3. Add salt to the fermented batter.
4. Heat a tawa/griddle, spread batter thinly in a circle.
5. Drizzle oil around the edges.
6. Cook until crispy and golden.
7. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Puttu and Kadala Curry
summary: Steamed rice and black chickpeas
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the onion. Cut into even-sized pieces.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add ground spices (turmeric, coriander, chili), stir well.
6. Add onion, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Idiyappam
summary: Steamed rice strings usually served with stew
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal separately for 6 hours.
2. Grind to a smooth batter, ferment overnight.
3. Add salt to the fermented batter.
4. Heat a tawa/griddle, spread batter thinly in a circle.
5. Drizzle oil around the edges.
6. Cook until crispy and golden.
7. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Olan
summary: White ash gourd and beans in coconut milk
instructions:
1. Wash and chop ash gourd.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add curry leaves — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add ash gourd, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until peas are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Kootu Curry
summary: Yam and plantain with roasted coconut
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the peas. Cut into even-sized pieces.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add pepper, stir well.
6. Add yam, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Inji Puli
summary: Ginger and tamarind sweet and sour pickle
instructions:
1. Peel and chop ginger into small pieces.
2. Heat sesame oil, add mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, and curry leaves.
3. Add the ginger and sauté for 5 minutes.
4. Add tamarind extract, jaggery, red chili powder, turmeric, and salt.
5. Simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes until thick and jam-like.
6. Cool completely and store — it keeps for weeks. Serve as a condiment with rice.

title: Nadan Chicken Curry
summary: Kerala style traditional chicken curry
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the chicken. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add ground spices (turmeric, coriander, chili), stir well.
6. Add chicken, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Meen Peera
summary: Small fish cooked with shredded coconut
instructions:
1. Cut fish into pieces, wash and drain.
2. Grind grated coconut with shallots, green chili, and turmeric to a coarse paste.
3. Place fish in a pan and spread the coconut mixture on top.
4. Add a splash of water, cover, and cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes.
5. Gently stir once, being careful not to break the fish.
6. Temper with coconut oil, mustard seeds, and curry leaves. Serve with rice.

title: Pathiri
summary: Thin rice pancakes from Malabar
instructions:
1. Mix rice flour with salt and enough boiling water to form a smooth dough.
2. Divide into small balls and roll each into a thin, round disc.
3. Cook each pathiri on a dry, hot tawa for about 30 seconds on each side.
4. The pathiri should remain soft and pliable — do not brown.
5. Stack and keep covered with a cloth to retain softness.
6. Serve warm with chicken curry or egg curry.

title: Nangia Curry
summary: Assamese fish curry with sour notes
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the fish. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add turmeric, stir well.
6. Add fish, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Khura
summary: Buckwheat pancakes from Arunachal
instructions:
1. Mix buckwheat flour with eggs, salt, and a little water to make a thin batter.
2. Heat butter in a flat pan or skillet.
3. Pour a thin layer of batter and spread evenly like a crepe.
4. Cook until the edges start to crisp and the bottom is golden.
5. Flip and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes.
6. Fold and serve hot with butter, cheese, or chili sauce.

title: Zan
summary: Monpa style porridge from Arunachal
instructions:
1. Bring water to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
2. Gradually add roasted barley flour (tsampa) while stirring continuously.
3. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon to prevent lumps.
4. Continue cooking and stirring until the mixture thickens and pulls away from the sides.
5. Add a knob of butter and mix in.
6. Shape into portions and serve as a staple accompaniment with meat or vegetable stew.

title: Eromba
summary: Manipuri fermented fish and vegetable mash
instructions:
1. Wash and chop potato.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add coriander, chili — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add potato, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until potato are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Morok Metpa
summary: Simple spicy chili chutney from Manipur
instructions:
1. Wash and chop onion.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add spices — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add onion, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until onion are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Ooti
summary: Manipuri pea and leafy green dish
instructions:
1. Wash and chop spinach.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Add cumin/mustard seeds for tempering.
4. Add onions and sauté until soft.
5. Add spices — turmeric, coriander, chili powder.
6. Add spinach, salt, and a splash of water.
7. Cover and cook until spinach, peas are tender.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve.

title: Sawhchiar
summary: Mizo meat and rice porridge
instructions:
1. Prepare chicken — clean, cut, and marinate with spices.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add chicken and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Koat Pitha
summary: Mizo banana and rice flour fritters
instructions:
1. Mash ripe bananas until smooth.
2. Mix mashed banana with rice flour, sugar, and a pinch of cardamom.
3. Add a little water if needed to make a thick, drop-able batter.
4. Heat oil in a pan for deep frying.
5. Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil and fry until golden brown on both sides.
6. Drain on paper towels and serve warm as a sweet snack.

title: Masor Tenga
summary: Assamese light and sour fish curry
instructions:
1. Prepare fish — clean, cut, and marinate with spices.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add fish and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Poora Haah
summary: Assamese roasted duck with bamboo shoot
instructions:
1. Clean and cut duck into serving pieces.
2. Marinate with mustard paste, turmeric, salt, and chili.
3. Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan, add the duck pieces and brown on all sides.
4. Add sliced onions, ginger-garlic paste, and cook until fragrant.
5. Add water, cover, and slow cook for 40-45 minutes until duck is tender.
6. Finish with black pepper and fresh coriander. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Khaar
summary: Assamese alkaline dish with papaya and pulses
instructions:
1. Wash and soak moong dal for 30 min.
2. Pressure cook moong dal with turmeric and water until soft.
3. Heat oil/ghee for tempering.
4. Add mustard seeds, cumin, and curry leaves.
5. Add chopped onion, garlic, tomato — sauté until soft.
6. Pour the tempering into the cooked moong dal.
7. Simmer for 5-10 min, adjust salt and consistency.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

title: Pad See Ew
summary: Thai stir-fried wide rice noodles
instructions:
1. Prepare beef — clean, cut, and marinate with spices.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add beef and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Green Curry
summary: Thai spicy and aromatic green coconut curry
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the chicken. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add basil, stir well.
6. Add chicken, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Massaman Curry
summary: Rich mild Thai curry with peanuts and potato
instructions:
1. Wash and prepare the beef. Cut into bite-sized pieces and marinate with a pinch of salt and turmeric for 10 minutes.
2. Heat oil/ghee, sauté sliced onions until golden.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook for 1 min.
4. Add tomatoes and cook until soft and oil separates.
5. Add ground spices (turmeric, coriander, chili), stir well.
6. Add beef, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

title: Som Tum
summary: Thai spicy green papaya salad
instructions:
1. Prepare shrimp — clean, cut, and marinate with spices.
2. Heat oil/ghee in a pan.
3. Sauté onions until translucent.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 1 min.
5. Add tomatoes and spices, cook until oil separates.
6. Add shrimp and mix well.
7. Add water if needed, cover and cook until done.
8. Garnish and serve hot with roti or rice.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
summary: Szechuan spicy stir-fry with peanuts
instructions:

title: Duck L'Orange
summary: Classic French roast duck with orange sauce
instructions:
1. Score the duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season with salt and pepper.
2. Place duck skin-side down in a cold pan, cook on medium until skin is crispy (8-10 min).
3. Flip and cook 4-5 min more. Rest for 10 minutes.
4. Make sauce: caramelize sugar, deglaze with orange juice and vinegar.
5. Add stock and reduce by half. Finish with butter and orange zest.
6. Slice duck, drizzle with orange sauce, and garnish with orange segments.

title: Starfruit and Chili Salad
summary: Exotic sharp and spicy tropical fruit salad
instructions:
1. Slice fresh starfruit into thin star-shaped pieces.
2. Thinly slice red chili and shallots.
3. Combine starfruit, chili, shallots, and fresh herbs (mint and cilantro) in a bowl.
4. Whisk together fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, and a dash of sesame oil for the dressing.
5. Toss the salad with the dressing.
6. Top with crushed peanuts and serve as a refreshing appetizer.

title: Dragon Fruit Smoothie Royale
summary: Exotic pink smoothie with superfoods
instructions:
1. Scoop out the flesh of pink and white dragon fruit. Freeze for 4 hours.
2. Blend frozen dragon fruit with frozen mango, yogurt, and a splash of coconut milk.
3. Blend until very thick and creamy.
4. Pour into a chilled bowl.
5. Top with sliced kiwi, passion fruit seeds, toasted coconut, and granola.
6. Drizzle with agave nectar and serve immediately.

title: Wild Berry Tart
summary: Delicate tart with foraged forest berries
instructions:
1. Make pastry: rub butter into flour, add sugar and egg yolk. Press into a tart tin and chill.
2. Blind bake the crust at 180°C for 15 minutes until golden.
3. Prepare filling: whisk cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla until smooth.
4. Spread the cream cheese filling into the cooled tart shell.
5. Arrange fresh wild berries (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries) on top.
6. Brush with warm apricot glaze for shine. Chill 30 min before serving.

title: Hibiscus Tea Poached Pears
summary: Elegant dessert with floral notes
instructions:
1. Gather all ingredients: pears, hibiscus tea, cinnamon and honey.
2. If using fresh fruits or vegetables, wash thoroughly and chop into small pieces.
3. Add pears and hibiscus tea to a blender or mixing glass.
4. Add water, milk, or ice as needed for your preferred consistency.
5. Blend until smooth (for shakes/smoothies) or stir well (for drinks).
6. Taste and adjust sweetness with sugar or honey. Add a pinch of salt to enhance flavor.
7. Strain through a fine sieve if you prefer a smooth texture.
8. Pour into serving glasses. Garnish with fresh mint, a slice of lemon, or crushed ice.
9. Serve immediately while fresh and chilled.

title: Candied Lotus Seeds
summary: Rare traditional delicate sweet snack
instructions:
1. Rinse lotus seeds (makhana) and pat dry.
2. Dry roast lotus seeds in a pan until crisp and crunchy (8-10 min on low heat).
3. In a separate pan, melt jaggery or sugar with a tablespoon of ghee.
4. Add cardamom powder to the melted sugar.
5. Add the roasted lotus seeds and toss until evenly coated.
6. Spread on parchment paper, let cool and harden. Break apart and serve.

title: Pindi Chole Masala
summary: Spicy dark chickpeas with tangy amchur

5. Add ground spices (turmeric, coriander, chili), stir well.
6. Add main ingredient, coat with the masala.
7. Add water as needed, cover and simmer until cooked through.
8. Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti/rice.

instructions:

3. Heat oil/ghee for tempering.
4. Add mustard seeds, cumin, and curry leaves.
5. Add chopped onion, garlic, tomato — sauté until soft.
6. Pour the tempering into the cooked arhar dal.
7. Simmer for 5-10 min, adjust salt and consistency.
8. Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.

instructions:

2. Heat oil or ghee in a suitable pan over medium heat.
3. Add aromatics — finely chopped onion, garlic, and ginger. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
4. Add fennel, pepper and saffron and stir for 30 seconds to bloom the flavors.
5. Add milk and almonds and cook according to the method — stir occasionally to ensure even cooking.
6. Add water or stock as needed. Cover and cook until milk and almonds is tender and fully cooked through.
7. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and any finishing spices.
8. Serve hot, garnished with fresh herbs and accompanied by rice, bread, or your preferred side.

title: Iced Matcha Latte
summary: Energy-boosting green tea latte served over ice.
instructions:
1. Sift 1-2 teaspoons of matcha powder into a bowl to remove lumps.
2. Add a splash of hot water (not boiling — 80°C) and whisk vigorously with a bamboo whisk until frothy.
3. Sweeten with honey or simple syrup to taste.
4. Fill a glass with ice cubes.
5. Pour cold milk of your choice over the ice.
6. Pour the matcha concentrate over the milk. Stir and enjoy.

title: Green Detox Juice

instructions:
1. Combine frozen strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries in a blender.
2. Add a ripe banana for natural sweetness.
3. Pour in yogurt or almond milk.
4. Add a tablespoon of honey and a squeeze of lemon.
5. Blend on high until smooth and creamy.
6. Pour into a glass, garnish with fresh berries, and serve immediately.

title: Banana Oat Shake
summary: Filling breakfast shake with oats and honey.
instructions:
1. Peel and slice a ripe banana.
2. Add the banana, rolled oats, milk, and a spoonful of peanut butter to a blender.
3. Add honey or a medjool date for sweetness.
4. Add a pinch of cinnamon.
5. Blend on high until completely smooth.
6. Pour into a glass, sprinkle with a pinch of cinnamon, and serve chilled.

title: Jal Jeera
summary: Spicy and tangy Indian lemonade with cumin and mint.
instructions:
1. Soak cumin seeds, mint leaves, and tamarind in water for 30 minutes.
2. Blend soaked ingredients with fresh coriander, green chili, ginger, and black salt.
3. Strain through a fine sieve into a jug.
4. Add roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, and regular salt to taste.
5. Mix in chilled water and adjust flavors.
6. Serve cold in glasses with ice, garnished with mint and a slice of lemon.

title: Garlic Naan
summary: Leavened flatbread topped with garlic and butter.
instructions:
1. Mix flour with salt, water, and oil. Knead into soft dough.
2. Rest for 20 min covered with a damp cloth.
3. Divide into balls, roll out into circles.
4. Cook on hot tawa until brown spots appear on both sides.
5. Apply ghee/butter and serve hot.

title: Aloo Paratha
summary: Whole wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potatoes.
instructions:
1. Prepare potato stuffing — boil/grate and mix with spices.
2. Knead atta dough with water and salt, rest 20 min.
3. Roll dough, place potato filling, seal and re-roll.
4. Cook on hot tawa with ghee/oil until golden on both sides.
5. Serve hot with curd, pickle, or butter.

title: Mint Chutney

instructions:
1. Wash a large bunch of fresh mint leaves and coriander leaves. Remove thick stems.
2. In a blender, add mint, coriander, 2 green chilies, a small piece of ginger, and 2 cloves of garlic.
3. Add a squeeze of lemon juice, a pinch of cumin powder, and salt to taste.
4. Add 2-3 tablespoons of water and blend to a smooth, vibrant green paste.
5. Taste and adjust — add more chili for heat, lemon for tang, or salt as needed.
6. Transfer to a serving bowl. Serve fresh as a dip with samosa, tikka, or as a spread in sandwiches.
7. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.

title: Boondi Raita
summary: Cooling yogurt side with crispy chickpea flour pearls.
instructions:
1. If using packaged boondi, soak them in warm water for 5 minutes until they soften. Squeeze out excess water gently.
2. In a mixing bowl, whisk together fresh curd (yogurt) until smooth and creamy.
3. Add the softened boondi to the curd and mix gently.
4. Season with roasted cumin powder, chaat masala, salt, and a pinch of red chili powder.
5. Mix everything together. Add finely chopped coriander and a small piece of grated ginger.
6. Refrigerate for 15-20 minutes to let the flavors meld together.
7. Serve chilled as a side dish with biryani, pulao, or any spicy meal.

2. Grind or mix with the other ingredients.
3. Add salt, spices, and tempering if needed.
4. Mix well and adjust seasoning.
5. Serve as a side accompaniment.

title: Mango Pickle
summary: Traditional Indian spicy and sour raw mango pickle.
instructions:
1. Wash and dry raw mangoes thoroughly. Cut into small bite-sized pieces, discarding the seed.
2. In a dry pan, roast fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds, and fennel seeds until fragrant. Grind to a coarse powder.
3. In a large mixing bowl, combine the mango pieces with salt, turmeric, red chili powder, and the ground spice mix.
4. Heat mustard oil until it reaches smoking point, then let it cool to lukewarm.
5. Pour the cooled oil over the spiced mango mixture. Mix thoroughly to coat every piece.
6. Transfer to a clean, dry glass jar. Press down to ensure the oil covers the mango pieces.
7. Cover loosely and keep in sunlight for 2-3 days, stirring once daily.
8. After 3 days, the pickle is ready to eat. Store in a cool, dry place for up to 6 months.

4. Add tomato puree and cook until oil separates.
5. Stir in cream, garam masala, and kasuri methi. Add cooked paneer.
6. Simmer 10 min on low heat. Garnish with cream and serve with naan.

title: Saag Chicken
summary: Saag-style chicken curry with aromatic Indian spices.
instructions:
1. Blanch spinach in boiling water 2 min, transfer to ice water, then blend smooth.
2. Heat oil, add cumin seeds, sauté onion, ginger, garlic, and green chili.
3. Add chopped tomato, cook until soft.
4. Pour in the spinach puree, stir well.
5. Add chicken pieces, simmer 15 min until cooked through.
6. Finish with a swirl of cream and garam masala. Serve with makki roti.

title: Masala Chicken
summary: Masala-style chicken curry with aromatic Indian spices.
instructions:
1. Heat oil, add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
2. Sauté finely chopped onion until golden brown.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 2 min until raw smell goes.
4. Add tomato, turmeric, coriander, and red chili powder. Cook until oil separates.
5. Add chicken, pour in half cup water, cover and cook 20 min.
6. Sprinkle garam masala, garnish with coriander. Serve hot.

summary: Chettinad-style chicken curry with aromatic Indian spices.
instructions:

2. Heat oil, add curry leaves and sauté onion until brown.
3. Add ginger-garlic paste and tomato. Cook until mushy.
4. Add the roasted spice-coconut paste and mix well.

6. Thick, aromatic gravy should coat the chicken. Serve with parotta.

title: Rogan Josh Chicken

instructions:
1. Heat oil, add whole spices (cardamom, cloves, bay leaf).
2. Add sliced onion and cook until deep golden.

4. Add chicken and sear on high heat for 5 min.
5. Stir in beaten curd (one spoon at a time to prevent curdling), add water.
6. Slow cook covered for 30 min until tender. Rich red gravy, serve with rice.

title: Malai Chicken
summary: Malai-style chicken curry with aromatic Indian spices.
instructions:
1. Soak cashews, grind with a little milk to smooth paste.
2. Melt butter, sauté onion and ginger-garlic until soft (don't brown).
3. Add cashew paste, cardamom, and white pepper. Cook 5 min.
4. Add chicken and half cup milk. Simmer gently 15 min.
5. Stir in fresh cream, cook 5 more min on very low heat.
6. Mild, creamy, and aromatic. Serve with butter naan.

2. Heat oil, add curry leaves and sliced onion. Fry until crisp brown.
3. Add ginger-garlic, green chili, turmeric.
4. Add kofta, sear 5 min.
5. Stir in ground nut-coconut paste and beaten curd. Add water, simmer 20 min.
6. Rich Hyderabadi gravy — serve with biryani rice or roti.

title: Lucknowi Chicken
summary: Lucknowi-style chicken curry with aromatic Indian spices.
instructions:
1. Fry sliced onion in ghee until golden. Remove half for garnish.
2. Add cardamom, mace, and cashew paste to the remaining onion.
3. Add chicken and sear lightly.
4. Stir in beaten curd and saffron-infused milk.
5. Cook on dum (sealed low heat) for 25 min.
6. Finish with rose water and cream. Garnish with fried onions. Serve with roomali roti.

title: Dhaba Style Chicken
summary: Dhaba Style-style chicken curry with aromatic Indian spices.
instructions:

3. Add ginger-garlic, cook 3 min.
4. Add lots of tomato, mash and cook until thick.
5. Add chicken, all spices, and water. Cook on high heat 20 min.
6. Rustic and bold flavors — serve with thick tandoori roti.

5. Add chicken and tamarind water. Simmer 20 min.
6. Coastal flavors with tangy heat. Serve with neer dosa.

title: Kashmiri Chicken
summary: Kashmiri-style chicken curry with aromatic Indian spices.
instructions:

3. Lower heat, add Kashmiri red chili and fennel powder.
4. Stir in beaten curd (one tablespoon at a time).
5. Add dry ginger powder and water. Simmer 25 min.
6. Minimal but aromatic — bright red Kashmiri gravy. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Plain Dosa
summary: Classic South Indian plain dosa — crispy and delicious.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and urad dal separately for 6 hours.
2. Grind to smooth batter, mix, add salt. Ferment overnight.
3. Heat a flat tawa, spread thin layer of batter in circular motion.
4. Drizzle oil around edges.
5. Cook until crisp and golden brown underneath.
6. Fold and serve with sambar and coconut chutney.

title: Onion Uttapam
summary: Classic South Indian onion uttapam — crispy and delicious.
instructions:
1. Prepare thick dosa batter (fermented overnight).
2. Chop onion, tomato, green chili, and coriander finely.
3. Pour thick layer of batter on hot tawa.
4. Sprinkle chopped onion, tomato on top, press gently.
5. Cook on medium heat until bottom is golden, flip carefully.
6. Cook other side 2 min. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Set Dosa
summary: Classic South Indian set dosa — crispy and delicious.
instructions:
1. Prepare dosa batter with extra urad dal for fluffiness. Ferment overnight.
2. Add a pinch of sugar and baking soda to the batter.
3. Heat tawa on low, pour small thick rounds of batter.
4. Cover and cook — don't flip. Steam cooks the top.
5. Remove soft, spongy dosas when cooked through.
6. Serve as a set of 3 with vegetable sagu and chutney.

title: Neer Dosa
summary: Classic South Indian neer dosa — crispy and delicious.
instructions:
1. Soak rice for 4 hours. Grind with grated coconut and water to thin batter.
2. No fermentation needed — batter should be very watery.
3. Heat a non-stick pan, pour batter and swirl quickly.
4. Cover and cook 1 min on low heat — edges will lift.
5. Gently peel off the delicate, lacy dosa.
6. Serve with chicken curry or coconut milk curry. Mangalorean specialty.

title: Pesarattu
summary: Classic South Indian pesarattu — crispy and delicious.
instructions:
1. Soak green moong dal and rice (4:1 ratio) for 4 hours.
2. Grind with ginger, green chili, cumin, and salt to thick batter.
3. No fermentation needed.
4. Spread batter on hot tawa like a dosa.
5. Top with chopped onion, press down. Cook until crisp.
6. Fold and serve with ginger chutney. Andhra Pradesh specialty.

title: Tamarind Rice
summary: Traditional South Indian tamarind rice — flavorful one-pot rice.
instructions:
1. Cook rice and cool completely.
2. Soak tamarind, extract thick pulp.
3. Heat sesame oil, add mustard seeds, urad dal, peanuts, red chili, curry leaves.
4. Add tamarind pulp, turmeric, salt. Cook until thick paste forms.
5. Mix the tamarind paste thoroughly with cooled rice.
6. Tangy and spicy — serve with appalam. Great for travel.

title: Bisibele Bath
summary: Traditional South Indian bisibele bath — flavorful one-pot rice.
instructions:
1. Cook rice and toor dal together until soft.
2. Boil mixed vegetables (beans, carrot, peas) separately.
3. Extract tamarind juice. Combine rice-dal, vegetables, tamarind.
4. Add bisibele bath powder and salt. Simmer 10 min.
5. Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, cashews in ghee.
6. Pour over bisibele bath. Serve hot with boondi raita.

title: Pongal
summary: Traditional South Indian pongal — flavorful one-pot rice.
instructions:
1. Dry roast moong dal until golden.
2. Cook rice and dal together with extra water until very soft and mushy.
3. Crush black pepper and cumin coarsely.
4. Heat ghee, fry cashews, pepper-cumin, ginger, curry leaves.
5. Pour tempering into the rice-dal mixture, stir well.
6. Ven Pongal should be creamy and peppery. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Puliyodarai
summary: Traditional South Indian puliyodarai — flavorful one-pot rice.
instructions:
1. Cook rice, cool and separate grains.
2. Make paste: roast sesame, peanuts, fenugreek, red chili. Grind coarse.
3. Cook tamarind extract with the ground paste and turmeric until thick.
4. Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves in sesame oil. Add to paste.
5. Mix the puliyodarai paste with rice. Use as much paste as preferred.
6. Flavors improve the next day. Classic temple prasadam.

title: Pepper Rasam
summary: Authentic pepper rasam — a South Indian staple.
instructions:
1. Cook toor dal soft, extract thin dal water.
2. Crush lots of black pepper and cumin coarsely.
3. Boil tamarind water with tomato, crushed pepper-cumin, and garlic.
4. Add dal water, bring to a rolling boil.
5. As soon as it froths up, remove from heat.
6. Add a teaspoon of ghee. Excellent cold remedy — serve piping hot.

title: Mysore Rasam
summary: Authentic mysore rasam — a South Indian staple.
instructions:
1. Roast red chili, coconut, coriander, and cumin. Grind to paste.
2. Cook toor dal, extract thin water.
3. Add tamarind extract and tomato to dal water.
4. Add the ground paste, bring to a boil.
5. Simmer 5 min until flavors meld.
6. Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves. Spicier than regular rasam.

title: Idli
summary: South Indian idli — perfect breakfast or snack.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and urad dal with fenugreek seeds separately for 6 hours.
2. Grind urad dal first to fluffy batter, then rice to slightly coarse batter.
3. Mix both, add salt. Ferment 8-12 hours until doubled.
4. Grease idli moulds, pour batter into each.
5. Steam for 12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
6. Soft and fluffy idlis — serve hot with sambar and chutney.

title: Mini Idli Fry
summary: South Indian mini idli fry — perfect breakfast or snack.
instructions:
1. Make small idlis using mini idli plates.
2. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and peanuts.
3. Add chopped onion and green chili, sauté until golden.
4. Toss in the mini idlis, stir on high heat.
5. Add a pinch of turmeric and chili powder.
6. Crunchy outside, soft inside — great evening snack.

title: Vegetable Stew
summary: Vegetable Stew — mildly spiced South Indian comfort food.
instructions:
1. Cut potato, carrot, beans into even pieces.
2. Heat coconut oil, add cinnamon, cloves, and curry leaves.
3. Add slit green chili and sliced ginger.
4. Add potato, carrot, beans, cook 5 min.
5. Pour thin coconut milk, simmer until potato, carrot, beans are tender.
6. Add thick coconut milk, heat through without boiling. Serve with appam.

title: Egg Stew
summary: Egg Stew — mildly spiced South Indian comfort food.
instructions:
1. Hard boil eggs, peel and make slits on surface.
2. Heat coconut oil, add whole spices and curry leaves.
3. Sauté sliced onion, ginger, green chili until soft.
4. Add potato pieces and thin coconut milk. Cook until potato is tender.
5. Add thick coconut milk and boiled eggs.
6. Simmer 5 min without boiling. Kerala-style — serve with appam or idiyappam.

title: Chicken Stew
summary: Chicken Stew — mildly spiced South Indian comfort food.
instructions:
1. Cut chicken into pieces. Slice potato, onion, carrot.
2. Heat coconut oil, add cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, curry leaves.
3. Sauté onion and ginger until fragrant.
4. Add chicken, cook until it turns white.
5. Add potato, onion, carrot and thin coconut milk. Simmer 20 min.
6. Add thick coconut milk last. Gentle, mildly spiced — serve with appam.

title: Vegetable Kurma
summary: Vegetable Kurma — mildly spiced South Indian comfort food.
instructions:
1. Grind coconut, cashew, and poppy seeds to smooth paste.
2. Heat oil, sauté onion until golden. Add ginger-garlic.
3. Add tomato, cook until soft.
4. Add potato, onion, tomato and half cup water, cook until tender.
5. Stir in the coconut-cashew paste. Simmer 10 min.
6. Thick, creamy korma — serve with parotta or biryani.

title: Tandoori Chicken
summary: Smoky grilled chicken marinated in aromatic spices.
instructions:
1. Make marinade: mix curd, red chili, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, lemon, salt.
2. Coat chicken thoroughly. Marinate 4 hours (overnight best).
3. Thread onto skewers or place on a rack.
4. Cook in oven at 230°C for 15-20 min, turning once.
5. Baste with oil or butter halfway through.
6. Charred and smoky — serve with mint chutney and onion rings.

title: Tandoori Paneer
summary: Smoky grilled paneer marinated in aromatic spices.
instructions:
1. Make marinade: mix curd, red chili, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, garam masala, lemon, salt.

title: Hariyali Chicken
summary: Smoky grilled chicken marinated in aromatic spices.
instructions:

3. Marinate chicken in the green mixture for 3 hours.
4. Skewer and grill at 220°C for 12-15 min.
5. The chicken should have a vibrant green crust.
6. Bright, herby flavors — serve with green chutney.

title: Malai Tikka Chicken
summary: Smoky grilled chicken marinated in aromatic spices.
instructions:
1. Mix cream, grated cheese, curd, cashew paste, cardamom, white pepper.
2. Add ginger-garlic paste and salt.
3. Coat chicken pieces in the creamy marinade. Rest 2 hours.
4. Skewer and cook at 200°C for 12 min — don't overcook.
5. The coating should be creamy white, not charred.
6. Mildly spiced and rich — serve with butter naan.

title: Reshmi Kebab Chicken
summary: Smoky grilled chicken marinated in aromatic spices.
instructions:
1. Mince or finely chop chicken.
2. Mix with cream, cashew paste, egg, ginger-garlic, mace, cardamom.
3. Shape into flat round kebabs on skewers.
4. Grill on medium heat, turning gently — they're delicate.
5. Cook 8-10 min until golden but still moist inside.
6. Silky smooth texture — serve with roomali roti and mint chutney.
