title: Shorshe Maach
summary: Authentic Bengali shorshe maach — rich in tradition.
instructions:
1. Coat fish pieces with turmeric and salt.
2. Fry lightly in mustard oil until golden. Set aside.
3. Grind mustard seeds with green chili and a little water to paste.
4. Heat mustard oil, add the mustard paste, cook 3 min.
5. Add water, bring to simmer. Add fried fish.
6. Cook covered 10 min. Pungent mustard gravy — serve with steamed rice.

title: Aloo Posto
summary: Authentic Bengali aloo posto — rich in tradition.
instructions:
1. Soak poppy seeds in water for 30 min. Grind to smooth paste.
2. Cut potatoes into cubes.
3. Heat mustard oil, fry potatoes with turmeric until golden.
4. Add poppy seed paste and green chili.
5. Add a splash of water, cover and cook 10 min on low.
6. Creamy poppy seed coating on potatoes. Bengali comfort food with rice.

title: Chingri Malaikari
summary: Authentic Bengali chingri malaikari — rich in tradition.
instructions:
1. Clean shrimp, marinate with turmeric and salt.
2. Fry shrimp lightly in ghee, set aside.
3. In same ghee, add bay leaf, cardamom, sliced onion. Sauté until golden.
4. Add ginger paste and a pinch of sugar.
5. Pour coconut milk, bring to gentle simmer. Add shrimp.
6. Cook 8 min on low. Rich, sweet, and creamy — serve with steamed rice.

title: Baingan Bhaja
summary: Authentic Bengali begun bhaja — rich in tradition.
instructions:
1. Slice brinjal into thin rounds.
2. Mix turmeric, red chili powder, and salt.
3. Coat each brinjal slice with the spice mix.
4. Heat mustard oil in a pan.
5. Shallow fry slices until crispy and golden on both sides.
6. Simple and addictive — serve as a side with dal and rice.

title: Luchi Aloo Dum
summary: Authentic Bengali luchi aloo dum — rich in tradition.
instructions:
1. Knead maida with ghee, salt, water into soft dough. Rest 30 min.
2. Make aloo dum: fry cubed potato, add ginger, cumin, tomato, turmeric.
3. Add water, simmer until potato is tender and gravy thickens.
4. Roll small balls of dough into thin circles.
5. Deep fry in hot oil until puffed and golden.
6. Soft, puffy luchi with spicy aloo dum — Bengali Sunday breakfast.

title: Kosha Mangsho
summary: Authentic Bengali kosha mangsho — rich in tradition.
instructions:
1. Marinate mutton with curd, ginger-garlic paste, and spices for 2 hours.
2. Heat mustard oil until smoking, then cool slightly.
3. Add sliced onion, fry until very dark brown.
4. Add marinated mutton, cook on high heat stirring often.
5. Add minimal water, cook covered on low for 45-50 min.
6. Dry, dark, intensely flavored — the mutton should fall off the bone.

title: Phuchka
summary: Authentic Bengali phuchka — rich in tradition.
instructions:
1. Make puris: knead semolina dough, roll tiny circles, deep fry until puffed.
2. Boil and mash potato. Mix with boiled chickpeas, cumin, chili, salt.
3. Make tamarind water: dissolve tamarind with cumin, black salt, chili.
4. Also make mint water with coriander, mint, green chili.
5. Crack a hole in each puri, stuff with potato-chickpea filling.
6. Dip in tamarind water and eat whole. Kolkata street food at its best.

title: Dhokla
summary: Classic Gujarati dhokla — sweet, sour, and spiced.
instructions:
1. Mix gram flour with curd, turmeric, salt, sugar, and water to smooth batter.
2. Add eno or baking soda, mix quickly.
3. Pour into greased plate, steam 15 min until spongy.
4. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chili.
5. Add water, sugar, lemon juice to the tempering.
6. Pour tempering over cut dhokla pieces. Garnish with coriander and coconut.

title: Khandvi
summary: Classic Gujarati khandvi — sweet, sour, and spiced.
instructions:
1. Mix gram flour with curd, turmeric, ginger-chili paste, water, salt.
2. Cook on low heat stirring continuously 15-20 min until very thick.
3. Quickly spread thin layer on greased surface (back of thali).
4. Let cool 5 min, then roll up tightly into scrolls.
5. Cut into pieces. Temper with mustard seeds, sesame.
6. Garnish with coconut and coriander. Melt-in-mouth texture.

title: Undhiyu
summary: Classic Gujarati undhiyu — sweet, sour, and spiced.
instructions:
1. Stuff small brinjals with coconut-peanut-spice filling.
2. Layer all potato, brinjal, sweet potato in a heavy pot.
3. Add green masala (coriander, coconut, chili, ginger ground paste).
4. Pour oil, cover tightly, cook on low heat 30-40 min.
5. Turn carefully once. potato, brinjal, sweet potato should be tender but not mushy.
6. Mixed vegetable medley — iconic Gujarati winter dish. Serve with puri.

title: Gujarati Kadhi
summary: Classic Gujarati gujarati kadhi — sweet, sour, and spiced.
instructions:
1. Whisk curd and gram flour with water until smooth (no lumps).
2. Add turmeric, salt, and sugar.
3. Bring to boil stirring constantly, then simmer 20 min.
4. Heat ghee, add mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves, dried chili.
5. Pour tempering into kadhi.
6. Sweet, tangy, and thin — uniquely Gujarati. Serve hot over rice.

title: Handvo
summary: Classic Gujarati handvo — sweet, sour, and spiced.
instructions:
1. Soak rice, chana dal, toor dal together 4 hours. Grind to batter. Ferment overnight.
2. Grate bottle gourd, squeeze water. Mix into batter.
3. Add ginger, chili, turmeric, salt.
4. Heat oil in a pan, add sesame, mustard seeds. Pour batter.
5. Cover and cook on low heat 20 min. Flip carefully.
6. Savory cake — crispy outside, soft inside. Serve with green chutney.

title: Gatte Ki Sabzi
summary: Traditional Rajasthani gatte ki sabzi from the desert state.
instructions:
1. Mix gram flour with cumin, chili, turmeric, salt, oil. Knead into dough.
2. Roll into long cylinders. Boil in water 15 min. Slice into pieces.
3. Heat oil, add cumin, sauté ginger.
4. Add curd whisked with gram flour, turmeric, chili. Cook 5 min.
5. Add boiled gatte pieces to the curd gravy.
6. Simmer 10 min. Classic Rajasthani vegetarian dish — serve with roti.

title: Bajra Roti
summary: Traditional Rajasthani bajra roti from the desert state.
instructions:
1. Heat water with salt. Add bajra flour gradually, mix.
2. Knead into soft dough while warm (bajra is hard to roll cold).
3. Pat into thick rounds using palms (don't use rolling pin).
4. Cook on tawa on medium heat, both sides.
5. Hold directly over flame briefly to puff.
6. Apply generous ghee. Serve hot with ker sangri or garlic chutney.

title: Pyaaz Kachori
summary: Traditional Rajasthani pyaaz kachori from the desert state.
instructions:
1. Filling: fry chopped onion until brown. Add cumin, fennel, coriander, chili, amchur.
2. Dough: mix maida with oil and water. Knead smooth. Rest 30 min.
3. Roll small circles, place filling, seal and shape into balls.
4. Flatten slightly. Deep fry on low heat until golden (slow frying = crispy).
5. Fry 8-10 min total, turning often.
6. Crispy, flaky, spicy — serve with tamarind and green chutney.

title: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic hyderabadi chicken biryani — layered rice perfection.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken with curd, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, salt for 2 hours.
2. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices until 70% done. Drain.
3. Fry sliced onion until deep golden. Reserve half.
4. Layer marinated chicken, then rice, then fried onion, mint, saffron milk.
5. Seal pot with dough, cook on dum (very low heat) for 25 min.
6. Break seal, gently mix layers. Serve with mirchi ka salan and raita.

title: Thalassery Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic thalassery chicken biryani — layered rice perfection.
instructions:
1. Cook chicken with ground spices, coconut milk until tender.
2. Cook kaima (short-grain) rice separately until each grain is separate.
3. Fry cashews, raisins, sliced onion in ghee.
4. Layer rice and chicken masala alternately.
5. Top with fried garnish. Give dum 15 min.
6. Malabar specialty — uses short grain rice, not basmati. Serve with raita.

title: Dindigul Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic dindigul chicken biryani — layered rice perfection.
instructions:
1. Cook chicken with tomato, ginger-garlic, and fennel-heavy masala.
2. Use seeraga samba rice (jeera rice) — wash and soak 20 min.
3. Add rice directly to the chicken gravy with measured water.
4. Cook covered until rice absorbs all liquid.
5. Garnish with fried onion and mint.
6. One-pot style, peppery and tangy. Tamil Nadu biryani — serve with brinjal curry.

title: Chicken Pulao
summary: Aromatic chicken pulao — layered rice perfection.
instructions:
1. Soak basmati rice 20 min.
2. Heat ghee, add cumin, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves.
3. Sauté onion until golden, add ginger-garlic.
4. Add chicken and tomato. Cook 5 min.
5. Add drained rice and water (1:1.5 ratio). Season with salt.
6. Cook covered on low heat until rice is fluffy. Serve with raita.

title: Chicken Tahiri
summary: Aromatic chicken tahiri — layered rice perfection.
instructions:

2. Heat oil, add cumin, cloves, cinnamon. Fry onion until golden.
3. Add chicken and green chili. Sauté 5 min.
4. Add turmeric, salt, drained rice, and water.
5. Cook covered on low until rice is done.
6. Simple yellow rice — aromatic and comforting. Serve with raita or curry.

title: Dal Tadka
summary: Comforting dal tadka — protein-rich Indian lentils.
instructions:
1. Cook toor dal with turmeric and salt until soft. Mash lightly.
2. Heat ghee, add cumin, mustard seeds, garlic, dried red chili.
3. Add chopped onion, sauté until golden.
4. Add tomato, cook until soft.
5. Pour this tadka over the cooked dal, stir.
6. Garnish with coriander. Simple, everyday dal — serve with rice or roti.

title: Chana Dal
summary: Comforting chana dal — protein-rich Indian lentils.
instructions:
1. Soak chana dal 2 hours. Pressure cook until just soft (not mushy).
2. Heat ghee, add cumin seeds.
3. Sauté onion until golden, add ginger, green chili.
4. Add tomato and turmeric, cook until soft.
5. Add cooked chana dal, simmer 10 min.
6. Thicker than toor dal — nutty flavor. Serve with puri or rice.

title: Masoor Dal
summary: Comforting masoor dal — protein-rich Indian lentils.
instructions:
1. Wash masoor dal — no soaking needed.
2. Cook with turmeric, salt, and water until soft (15 min).
3. Heat mustard oil, add cumin, garlic, dried red chili.
4. Add onion, fry until brown. Add tomato.
5. Pour tempering into dal. Simmer 5 min.
6. Quick-cooking red lentils — earthy and wholesome. Serve with rice.

title: Palak Dal
summary: Comforting palak dal — protein-rich Indian lentils.
instructions:
1. Cook moong dal until soft.
2. Blanch spinach, blend to puree.
3. Mix spinach puree into cooked dal.
4. Heat ghee, sauté cumin, garlic, onion, tomato.
5. Pour tempering into palak dal. Simmer 10 min.
6. Iron-rich and nutritious — vivid green color. Serve with jeera rice.

title: Dal Dhokli
summary: Comforting dal dhokli — protein-rich Indian lentils.
instructions:
1. Make toor dal with turmeric. Add peanuts, jaggery, tamarind for sweet-sour taste.
2. Knead wheat flour dough with turmeric, chili, salt.
3. Roll thin, cut into diamond shapes (dhokli).
4. Drop dhokli directly into simmering dal.
5. Cook 10 min until dhokli is done.
6. Gujarati one-pot meal — dal and pasta combined. Comfort food.

title: Naan
summary: Fresh homemade naan — Indian bread done right.
instructions:
1. Mix maida, curd, sugar, baking soda, salt. Add egg.
2. Knead into soft, smooth dough. Rest 2 hours.
3. Divide into balls, roll into teardrop shapes.
4. Stick on the inside wall of a hot tandoor (or cook on inverted tawa).
5. Cook until bubbly and charred spots appear.
6. Brush with ghee. Soft and pillowy — perfect with any curry.

title: Stuffed Aloo Paratha
summary: Fresh homemade stuffed aloo paratha — Indian bread done right.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potatoes. Mix with onion, chili, cumin, amchur, coriander, salt.
2. Knead wheat flour into soft dough. Rest 20 min.
3. Take a dough ball, flatten, place potato filling, seal, and roll carefully.
4. Cook on hot tawa.
5. Apply ghee on both sides, cook until golden and crispy.
6. Punjabi breakfast staple — serve with curd, butter, and pickle.

title: Stuffed Gobi Paratha
summary: Fresh homemade stuffed gobi paratha — Indian bread done right.
instructions:
1. Grate cauliflower, squeeze out all water. Mix with ginger, chili, cumin, amchur, salt.
2. Knead wheat flour dough. Rest 20 min.
3. Stuff cauliflower filling into dough balls, roll into rounds.
4. Cook on tawa, apply ghee on both sides.
5. Press edges to cook evenly — golden spots should appear.
6. Crispy outside, spiced gobi inside — serve with pickle and curd.

title: Makki Ki Roti
summary: Fresh homemade makki ki roti — Indian bread done right.
instructions:
1. Mix corn flour with salt and warm water. Knead into dough.
2. Pat into thick rounds using hands (corn flour doesn't roll well).
3. Cook on hot tawa on low heat — corn takes longer.
4. Flip when set, apply ghee.
5. Cook until golden on both sides with slight char.
6. Pair with sarson ka saag — iconic Punjabi winter meal.

title: Sev Puri
summary: Crunchy sev puri — beloved Indian street food.
instructions:
1. Arrange flat puris on a plate.
2. Top each with finely chopped onion, tomato, boiled potato.
3. Drizzle tamarind chutney and green chutney.
4. Sprinkle chaat masala and salt.
5. Top generously with fine sev.
6. Garnish with coriander. Mumbai street food — sweet, tangy, crunchy.

title: Pakora
summary: Crunchy pakora — beloved Indian street food.
instructions:
1. Slice onion, potato thin. Keep spinach leaves whole.
2. Make batter: gram flour, cumin, chili, ajwain, salt, little water (thick).
3. Dip potato, onion, spinach in batter.
4. Deep fry in hot oil until golden and crispy.
5. Drain on paper towels.
6. Serve hot with mint chutney. Perfect with chai on rainy days.

title: Paneer Tikka Chaat
summary: Crunchy paneer tikka chaat — beloved Indian street food.
instructions:
1. Cube paneer and onion, bell pepper. Marinate in spiced curd.
2. Thread on skewers, grill until charred.
3. Remove from skewers, place in a bowl.
4. Drizzle mint and tamarind chutney.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala and squeeze lemon.
6. Fusion chaat — smoky meets tangy. Garnish with coriander and sev.

title: Kung Pao Beef
summary: Wok-tossed beef in kung pao sauce.
instructions:
1. Cut beef into cubes, marinate with soy sauce and cornstarch.
2. Fry dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns in oil until fragrant.
3. Add beef, stir-fry on high heat until cooked.
4. Add garlic, ginger, stir 30 seconds.
5. Pour in sauce (soy, vinegar, sugar, cornstarch slurry). Toss with peanuts.
6. Garnish with spring onion. Spicy, sweet, and nutty — serve with steamed rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Chicken
summary: Wok-tossed chicken in sweet and sour sauce.
instructions:
1. Cut chicken into pieces, coat with cornstarch, deep fry until golden. Set aside.
2. Stir-fry bell pepper, onion, pineapple chunks briefly.
3. Make sauce: mix ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, cornstarch, water.
4. Pour sauce into the wok, bring to bubble.
5. Add fried chicken and onion, bell pepper, corn. Toss to coat evenly.
6. Glossy and tangy — serve immediately with fried rice.

title: Manchurian Chicken

instructions:

3. Add soy sauce, chili sauce, ketchup, vinegar.
4. Add a cornstarch slurry for gravy consistency.
5. Toss in the fried chicken balls. Coat well.
6. Garnish with spring onion. Indo-Chinese favorite — serve dry or with gravy.

title: Chicken Katsu
summary: Authentic Japanese chicken katsu.
instructions:
1. Pound chicken breast to even thickness.
2. Season with salt and pepper.
3. Dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg, coat with panko.
4. Deep fry at 170°C for 6-7 min until deep golden.
5. Drain, rest 2 min, slice into strips.
6. Serve on rice with shredded cabbage and tonkatsu sauce.

title: Onigiri
summary: Authentic Japanese onigiri.
instructions:
1. Cook sushi rice, season with salt while warm.
2. Prepare fillings: flake grilled salmon, or mix tuna with mayo.
3. Wet hands, place rice, make indent, add filling.
4. Shape into triangle pressing firmly.
5. Wrap bottom and sides with a strip of nori.
6. Portable Japanese rice balls — perfect for bento or snack.

title: Edamame
summary: Authentic Japanese edamame.
instructions:
1. Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
2. Add frozen edamame pods.
3. Boil 4-5 minutes until bright green and tender.
4. Drain and toss with sea salt.
5. Optional: toss with garlic, chili flakes, sesame oil.
6. Pop beans out of pods with your teeth. Classic Japanese appetizer.

title: Thai Green Curry Chicken
summary: Authentic thai green curry chicken with coconut milk.
instructions:
1. Heat oil, fry green curry paste 2 min until fragrant.
2. Add thick coconut milk, stir until oil separates.
3. Add chicken, cook 5 min.
4. Pour in thin coconut milk, add bamboo shoots and bell pepper.
5. Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, torn kaffir lime leaves.
6. Finish with Thai basil. Aromatic and creamy — serve with jasmine rice.

summary: Authentic massaman curry chicken with coconut milk.

title: Pad Thai Chicken
summary: Thai pad thai chicken — bold and balanced flavors.
instructions:
1. Soak rice noodles in warm water until pliable.
2. Heat oil in wok, cook chicken until done. Push aside.
3. Scramble egg in the wok.
4. Add noodles, tamarind sauce, fish sauce, sugar. Toss on high heat.
5. Add bean sprouts, toss 30 seconds.
6. Serve with crushed peanuts, lime wedge, and chili flakes. Thailand's national dish.

title: Thai Basil Chicken

instructions:

4. Toss in large handful of Thai basil. It wilts in seconds.
5. Fry an egg sunny-side-up separately.
6. Serve over rice, topped with fried egg. Pad krapao — Thai street food staple.

title: Larb Chicken
summary: Thai larb chicken — bold and balanced flavors.
instructions:
1. Cook minced chicken in a dry pan — no oil — breaking into crumbles.
2. Remove from heat. Add lime juice and fish sauce.
3. Toss with sliced shallot, chili, mint, coriander, spring onion.
4. Add toasted rice powder for nutty crunch.
5. Taste — should be sour, salty, spicy, herby.
6. Serve in lettuce cups. Thai/Lao salad — refreshing and bold.

title: Satay Chicken
summary: Thai satay chicken — bold and balanced flavors.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken strips in coconut milk, turmeric, lemongrass, cumin, coriander.
2. Thread onto bamboo skewers (soaked in water).
3. Grill on high heat 3-4 min per side until charred.
4. Make peanut sauce: cook peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce, chili, sugar.
5. Thin with lime juice and water.
6. Serve skewers with warm peanut sauce and cucumber relish.

title: Bibimbap Chicken
summary: Korean bibimbap chicken — spicy and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Cook rice. Prepare namul: blanch and season spinach, bean sprouts, carrot, zucchini separately with sesame oil, garlic, salt.
2. Cook chicken with soy sauce and garlic.
3. Arrange rice in bowl, top with each vegetable in sections.
4. Place chicken and a fried egg in the center.
5. Add a generous spoon of gochujang.
6. Mix everything together before eating. Korean harmony in a bowl.

title: Bibimbap Egg
summary: Korean bibimbap egg — spicy and satisfying.
instructions:

2. Cook egg with soy sauce and garlic.
3. Arrange rice in bowl, top with each vegetable in sections.
4. Place egg and a fried egg in the center.
5. Add a generous spoon of gochujang.
6. Mix everything together before eating. Korean harmony in a bowl.

title: Korean Fried Chicken
summary: Korean korean fried chicken — spicy and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Cut chicken into pieces. Coat in cornstarch and rice flour mixture.
2. Double fry: fry at 170°C until cooked, then fry again at 190°C until super crispy.
3. Make sauce: cook gochujang, soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger until thick.
4. Toss crispy chicken in the sticky sauce.
5. Sprinkle sesame seeds and spring onion.
6. Crunchy, spicy, sweet, addictive. Korean KFC — better than the original.

title: Bulgogi Chicken
summary: Korean bulgogi chicken — spicy and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Make marinade: blend pear, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, sugar.
2. Slice chicken very thin against the grain.
3. Marinate for at least 2 hours (overnight best).
4. Grill or pan-fry on very high heat — should caramelize, not stew.
5. Cook in batches — don't overcrowd the pan.
6. Garnish with sesame and spring onion. Serve with lettuce wraps and rice.

title: Tteokbokki Chicken
summary: Korean tteokbokki chicken — spicy and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Soak rice cakes in water if using dried ones.
2. Boil dashi stock with gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar.
3. Add rice cakes and cook until soft and chewy (5-7 min).
4. Add chicken and cook through.
5. Add fish cake slices and cabbage. Simmer 3 min.
6. Garnish with spring onion. Spicy, chewy Korean street food.

instructions:

3. Add chicken and cook 3 min.
4. Pour in water, add gochugaru and soy sauce.
5. Bring to a boil, add cubed tofu. Simmer 15 min.
6. Finish with spring onion. Serve bubbling hot with rice. Korean comfort stew.

title: Sundubu Jjigae Chicken
summary: Korean sundubu jjigae chicken — spicy and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Make anchovy stock (or use dashi).
2. Sauté garlic, gochugaru, and kimchi in sesame oil.
3. Add chicken and cook briefly.
4. Pour in stock, add onion, zucchini. Boil 10 min.
5. Gently slide in soft (silken) tofu — don't stir, it breaks.
6. Crack an egg into the bubbling stew. Serve immediately with rice.

title: Pho Bo
summary: Vietnamese pho bo — fresh and vibrant.
instructions:
1. Char onion and ginger under broiler until blackened.
2. Simmer beef bones with charred aromatics, star anise, cinnamon, cloves for 3-4 hours.
3. Strain broth, season with fish sauce and salt.
4. Cook rice noodles separately.
5. Place noodles in bowl, top with thin raw beef slices.
6. Pour boiling broth over — it cooks the beef. Serve with basil, sprouts, lime, hoisin.

title: Pho Ga
summary: Vietnamese pho ga — fresh and vibrant.
instructions:
1. Simmer whole chicken with charred onion, ginger, coriander seeds.
2. Cook 45 min until chicken is tender. Remove, shred meat.
3. Strain broth, season with fish sauce.
4. Cook rice noodles.
5. Place noodles, shredded chicken in bowl, pour hot broth.
6. Serve with bean sprouts, basil, lime, chili. Lighter than beef pho.

title: Ca Kho To
summary: Vietnamese ca kho to — fresh and vibrant.
instructions:
1. Make caramel: cook sugar in a clay pot until dark amber.
2. Add fish sauce, coconut water carefully (it splatters).
3. Add garlic, shallot, chili, black pepper.
4. Place catfish steaks in the caramel sauce.
5. Simmer on low heat 20-25 min, basting fish with sauce.
6. Fish should be dark, glossy, and salty-sweet. Serve with plain rice.

title: Carbonara Chicken
summary: Italian carbonara chicken — classic comfort.
instructions:
1. Cook spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve pasta water.
2. Cook chicken until golden and rendered.
3. Whisk egg yolks with grated pecorino and black pepper.
4. Drain pasta, toss with chicken off the heat.
5. Add egg mixture, toss quickly — residual heat cooks eggs into creamy sauce.
6. Add pasta water if needed. No cream in real carbonara. Serve immediately.

title: Lasagna Chicken
summary: Italian lasagna chicken — classic comfort.
instructions:

2. Make bechamel: butter, flour, milk, nutmeg.

4. Top with parmesan.
5. Bake at 190°C for 35-40 min until bubbly and golden.
6. Rest 10 min before slicing. Layers of comfort.

title: Caprese Salad
summary: Authentic Italian caprese salad.
instructions:
1. Slice fresh mozzarella and ripe tomatoes into even rounds.
2. Alternate tomato and mozzarella slices on a plate.
3. Tuck fresh basil leaves between slices.
4. Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil.
5. Season with flaky salt and cracked black pepper.
6. Optional: balsamic reduction drizzle. Colors of the Italian flag.

title: Focaccia
summary: Authentic Italian focaccia.
instructions:
1. Mix flour, yeast, salt, water, generous olive oil. Knead until smooth.
2. Let rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
3. Press into an oiled baking pan, dimple with fingers.
4. Pour more olive oil into the dimples. Top with rosemary and sea salt.
5. Rise 30 more min.
6. Bake at 220°C for 20-25 min until golden. Crispy outside, fluffy inside.

title: Crepes
summary: Classic French crepes — refined and rich.
instructions:
1. Whisk flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, sugar, vanilla, salt until smooth.
2. Rest batter 30 min — this is crucial for tender crepes.
3. Heat a non-stick pan, pour thin layer of batter, swirl quickly.
4. Cook 1 min until edges lift, flip delicately.
5. Cook 30 seconds on other side.
6. Fill with Nutella and banana, or lemon and sugar. Fold into quarters.

title: Croissant
summary: Classic French croissant — refined and rich.
instructions:
1. Make dough: flour, yeast, sugar, milk, salt. Chill 1 hour.
2. Pound cold butter into a flat rectangle.
3. Encase butter in dough. Perform 3 letter folds, chilling 30 min between each.
4. Roll out, cut into triangles.
5. Roll from base to tip into crescent shapes. Proof 1.5 hours.
6. Brush with egg wash. Bake at 200°C 15-18 min until deeply golden and flaky.

title: Crème Brûlée
summary: Classic French crème brûlée — refined and rich.
instructions:
1. Heat cream with split vanilla bean until just simmering.
2. Whisk egg yolks with sugar until pale.
3. Slowly pour hot cream into yolks (tempering). Strain.
4. Pour into ramekins. Bake in water bath at 150°C for 40-45 min.
5. Chill completely (at least 4 hours).
6. Sprinkle sugar on top, torch until caramelized. Crack through for the custard.

title: Chicken Tacos
summary: Mexican chicken tacos — bold and festive.
instructions:
1. Season chicken with cumin, chili powder, garlic, salt.
2. Cook chicken in a hot skillet until done and slightly charred.

instructions:

title: Beef Mac and Cheese
summary: American beef mac and cheese — hearty and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Cook macaroni until al dente.
2. Make cheese sauce: melt butter, add flour, pour in milk. Stir until thick.
3. Add cheddar, gruyere, mustard, paprika. Stir until smooth.
4. Cook beef separately, fold in with pasta.
5. Pour into baking dish, top with breadcrumbs and more cheese.
6. Bake at 200°C for 15 min until golden and bubbly. Ultimate comfort food.

title: Cajun Beef
summary: American cajun beef — hearty and satisfying.
instructions:

2. Sear in a hot cast iron until blackened.
3. Remove beef. Sauté onion, celery, bell pepper (the holy trinity).
4. Add garlic, tomato, thyme, cayenne.
5. Return beef, add a splash of stock. Simmer 15 min.
6. Serve over white rice. Louisiana heat and flavor.

title: Beef Chili

instructions:

4. Add crushed tomato and kidney beans.

6. Serve with sour cream, cheese, and cornbread. Texas-style.

title: Beef Steak
summary: American beef steak — hearty and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Bring beef to room temperature. Season generously with salt and pepper.
2. Heat cast iron until smoking. Add oil.
3. Sear beef — don't move it for 3-4 min until a crust forms.
4. Flip, add butter, garlic, rosemary, thyme.
5. Baste with melted butter for 2 min.
6. Rest 8-10 min before slicing. Perfect sear, juicy center.

title: Lamb Shawarma
summary: Lamb Shawarma — Middle Eastern flavors.
instructions:
1. Marinate lamb in yogurt, cumin, paprika, turmeric, garlic, lemon for 2 hours.
2. Cook on high heat — grill or pan-sear until charred edges.
3. Slice thin against the grain.
4. Make tahini sauce: tahini, lemon juice, garlic, water, salt.
5. Warm pita, stuff with lamb, tomato, onion, pickle, lettuce.
6. Drizzle tahini sauce generously. Middle Eastern street food king.

title: Chicken Kebab
summary: Chicken Kebab — Middle Eastern flavors.
instructions:
1. Mix minced chicken with grated onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, parsley, salt.
2. Shape onto flat metal skewers in long oval shapes.
3. Grill on high heat, turning once — 4-5 min per side.
4. The outside should be charred, inside juicy.
5. Serve on warm pita with sumac onion and parsley salad.
6. Squeeze lemon, drizzle tahini. Smoky and aromatic.

title: Chicken Mansaf
summary: Chicken Mansaf — Middle Eastern flavors.
instructions:
1. Soak jameed (dried yogurt), blend smooth and cook into sauce.
2. Cook chicken in jameed sauce with cardamom until tender.
3. Cook rice with turmeric and ghee.
4. Toast almonds and pine nuts in butter.
5. Layer: flatbread, rice, chicken, pour jameed sauce over.
6. Top with toasted nuts. Jordan's national dish — eat with your right hand.

title: Chicken Fattoush Bowl
summary: Chicken Fattoush Bowl — Middle Eastern flavors.
instructions:

2. Toast or fry pita pieces until crispy.
3. Chop lettuce, tomato, cucumber, radish.
4. Make dressing: lemon juice, olive oil, sumac, salt.
5. Toss tomato, radish, cucumber with dressing. Add pita chips and chicken.

title: Chicken Biryani Arabic
summary: Chicken Biryani Arabic — Middle Eastern flavors.
instructions:
1. Cook chicken with onion, garlic, and Arabic spices until tender.
2. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices.
3. Fry onion rings and almonds until golden.
4. Layer chicken and rice. Sprinkle saffron milk and raisins.
5. Cook on dum (sealed, very low heat) for 20 min.
6. Garnish with fried onions, almonds. Arabian-style — sweeter and milder.

title: Chicken Tagine
summary: Chicken Tagine — Middle Eastern flavors.
instructions:
1. Season chicken with cumin, ginger, saffron, cinnamon.
2. Brown chicken in olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot.
3. Add sliced onion, garlic, cook until soft.
4. Add preserved lemon, olives, honey, and water.
5. Cover and cook on low heat 35-40 min.
6. Garnish with cilantro. Moroccan slow-cooked stew — sweet and savory.

title: Chicken Hummus Bowl
summary: Chicken Hummus Bowl — Middle Eastern flavors.
instructions:
1. Make hummus: blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic, cumin, ice water until silky.
2. Cook chicken with paprika and cumin.
3. Spread hummus in a bowl, create a well.
4. Place chicken in the center.
5. Drizzle olive oil, sprinkle paprika and chopped parsley.
6. Serve with warm pita for dipping. Protein-loaded hummus bowl.

title: Souvlaki
summary: Mediterranean souvlaki — sun-kissed flavors.
instructions:
1. Cube chicken, marinate in lemon, oregano, garlic, olive oil 2 hours.
2. Thread onto skewers.
3. Grill on high heat 3-4 min per side.
4. Make tzatziki: grated cucumber, yogurt, garlic, dill.
5. Warm pita, stuff with grilled chicken, tomato, onion.
6. Drizzle tzatziki. Greek street food — fresh and herby.

title: Spanakopita
summary: Mediterranean spanakopita — sun-kissed flavors.
instructions:
1. Sauté onion until soft. Add chopped spinach, cook until wilted. Cool.
2. Mix with crumbled feta, beaten egg, dill, salt, pepper.
3. Brush phyllo sheets with melted butter, layer 6-8 sheets.
4. Spread spinach-feta filling.
5. Top with 6-8 more buttered phyllo sheets.
6. Score top, bake at 180°C for 35-40 min until golden and flaky.

title: Patatas Bravas
summary: Mediterranean patatas bravas — sun-kissed flavors.
instructions:
1. Cut potatoes into rough cubes. Par-boil 5 min.
2. Deep fry or roast at 220°C until crispy and golden.
3. Make brava sauce: sauté garlic, add tomato, paprika, cayenne. Blend smooth.
4. Make aioli: garlic, olive oil, lemon, egg yolk.
5. Pile crispy potatoes on a plate.
6. Drizzle both sauces. Spanish tapas essential — order another plate.

title: Tabbouleh
summary: Mediterranean tabbouleh — sun-kissed flavors.
instructions:
1. Soak bulgur wheat in hot water 15 min. Drain, squeeze dry.
2. Finely chop lots of parsley (it's the onion, not bulgur).
3. Chop mint, tomato, cucumber, spring onion finely.
4. Combine everything in a bowl.
5. Dress with generous lemon juice and olive oil. Season.
6. Let it sit 30 min before serving. Lebanese herby salad — mostly green.

title: Nasi Goreng Chicken
summary: Southeast Asian nasi goreng chicken.
instructions:
1. Cook rice ahead — day-old rice works best.
2. Fry shallot, garlic, chili, and shrimp paste until fragrant.
3. Add chicken, cook until done.
4. Add cold rice, toss on high heat.
5. Season with kecap manis (sweet soy). Stir-fry 3 min.
6. Top with fried egg and fried shallots. Indonesian fried rice — sweet and savory.

title: Rendang Chicken
summary: Southeast Asian rendang chicken.
instructions:
1. Grind chili, shallot, garlic, galangal, turmeric, lemongrass to paste.
2. Fry paste until fragrant and darkened.
3. Add chicken, sear in the paste.
4. Pour coconut milk, add kaffir lime leaves.
5. Simmer on low heat 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally, until dry and dark.
6. Rendang is done when coconut oil separates and coats the chicken. Intensely rich.

summary: Southeast Asian rendang beef.

1. Grind chili, shallot, garlic, galangal, turmeric, lemongrass to paste.
2. Fry paste until fragrant and darkened.
3. Add beef, sear in the paste.
4. Pour coconut milk, add kaffir lime leaves.
5. Simmer on low heat 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally, until dry and dark.
6. Rendang is done when coconut oil separates and coats the beef. Intensely rich.

title: Mee Goreng Chicken
summary: Southeast Asian mee goreng chicken.
instructions:
1. Boil yellow noodles briefly, drain.

4. Add cabbage and bean sprouts, stir-fry 1 min.
5. Add noodles, soy sauce, chili sauce, tomato sauce. Toss on high.
6. Push aside, scramble egg, mix in. Malaysian fried noodles — saucy and spicy.

title: Laksa Chicken
summary: Southeast Asian laksa chicken.
instructions:
1. Fry laksa paste with shrimp paste until very fragrant.
2. Add coconut milk and water. Bring to boil, simmer 15 min.
3. Cook chicken in the broth.
4. Cook rice noodles separately.
5. Place noodles in bowl, add chicken, bean sprouts, tofu puffs, halved egg.
6. Ladle hot laksa broth over. Squeeze lime. Rich, coconut-spicy soup.

title: Satay Chicken Malay
summary: Southeast Asian satay chicken malay.
instructions:
1. Blend lemongrass, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garlic, sugar to paste.
2. Marinate chicken strips in paste for 2 hours.
3. Thread onto bamboo skewers.
4. Grill over charcoal or high heat until charred.
5. Make peanut sauce: cook peanut butter, coconut milk, chili, soy, sugar.
6. Serve with peanut sauce, cucumber, and compressed rice (nasi impit).

title: Gado Gado Chicken
summary: Southeast Asian gado gado chicken.
instructions:
1. Boil potato, green beans, cabbage, bean sprouts separately. Keep crisp-tender.
2. Fry tofu until golden. Hard boil eggs.
3. Cook chicken with light seasoning.
4. Make peanut dressing: ground peanuts, kecap manis, chili, lime, water.
5. Arrange potato, beans, cabbage, chicken, tofu, egg on a plate.
6. Pour peanut dressing over. Indonesian salad — hearty and nutty.

title: Chicken Adobo
summary: Authentic chicken adobo.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaf, pepper for 1 hour.
2. Brown chicken in oil on all sides.
3. Pour in the marinade and a little water.
4. Bring to boil, then simmer covered 30-35 min.
5. Uncover, reduce sauce until thick and glossy.
6. The sauce should coat the chicken. Filipino national dish — tangy and savory.

title: Nasi Lemak
summary: Authentic nasi lemak.
instructions:
1. Cook rice with coconut milk, pandan leaf, and salt until fragrant.
2. Deep fry anchovies until crispy.
3. Roast peanuts until golden.
4. Make sambal: blend chili, shrimp paste, tamarind. Cook until thick.
5. Hard boil and halve eggs.
6. Serve coconut rice with anchovies, peanuts, egg, cucumber, sambal. Malaysia's breakfast.

title: Jollof Rice
summary: African jollof rice — bold and aromatic.
instructions:
1. Blend tomato, bell pepper, scotch bonnet, onion to smooth paste.
2. Heat oil, fry tomato paste until reduced and oil floats (20 min).
3. Add garlic, ginger, thyme, curry powder, bay leaf.
4. Add washed rice and chicken stock.
5. Cover tightly, cook on very low heat until rice is done (30 min).
6. Smoky party rice — bottom should be slightly burnt (that's the best part!).

title: Chicken Yassa
summary: African chicken yassa — bold and aromatic.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in lemon juice, sliced onion, mustard, garlic, chili overnight.
2. Remove chicken, grill or pan-fry until golden.
3. Cook the marinated onions slowly until very soft and caramelized.
4. Add the grilled chicken back to onions.
5. Add a splash of vinegar, bay leaf. Simmer 20 min.
6. Onion-lemon gravy coats the chicken. Senegalese classic — serve with rice.

title: Bobotie
summary: African bobotie — bold and aromatic.
instructions:
1. Soak bread in milk, squeeze out.
2. Brown mince with onion, garlic, curry powder, turmeric.
3. Mix in chutney, raisins, soaked bread, almonds.
4. Press into a baking dish. Tuck in bay leaves.
5. Make custard topping: beat egg with remaining milk. Pour over.
6. Bake at 180°C for 30 min until custard sets. South African cape classic.

title: Doro Wat
summary: African doro wat — bold and aromatic.
instructions:
1. Slow-cook diced onions dry (no oil) until deeply brown — 30 min.
2. Add nit'ir qibe (spiced butter), garlic, ginger.
3. Add berbere spice generously. Cook 5 min.
4. Add chicken, coat in sauce. Add water.
5. Simmer 45 min. Add peeled hard-boiled eggs in last 10 min.
6. Serve on injera — tear pieces and scoop. Ethiopian celebratory dish.

title: Bunny Chow
summary: African bunny chow — bold and aromatic.
instructions:
1. Cook chicken curry: brown chicken, add onion, ginger-garlic, tomato.
2. Add curry powder, garam masala, potato. Cook until tender.
3. Take a quarter loaf of white bread.
4. Hollow out the center (eat the removed bread with curry!).
5. Fill the bread bowl with hot chicken curry.
6. Durban street food — messy, spicy, and iconic. South African-Indian fusion.

title: Tagine Vegetable
summary: African tagine vegetable — bold and aromatic.
instructions:
1. Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil.
2. Add cumin, cinnamon, and harissa. Cook 1 min.
3. Add chopped eggplant, zucchini, tomato.
4. Add chickpeas, preserved lemon, and water.
5. Cover and cook on low heat 30-35 min until onion, tomato, peas are very tender.
6. Garnish with cilantro. North African vegetable stew — serve with couscous.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: Warming chicken noodle soup — soul in a bowl.
instructions:
1. Simmer broth with ginger, garlic, soy sauce for 15 min.
2. Cook chicken in the broth until done.
3. Cook noodles separately until tender.
4. Add bok choy to broth, cook 2 min.
5. Place noodles in bowl, ladle broth and chicken over.
6. Top with spring onion, chili oil, sesame. Comforting bowl.

title: Creamy Chicken Soup
summary: Warming creamy chicken soup — soul in a bowl.
instructions:

4. Blend soup until smooth. Return to heat.
5. Stir in cream and cooked chicken.
6. Season with thyme, salt, pepper. Velvety and rich.

1. Make wonton filling: mix shrimp with ginger, garlic, soy, sesame oil.
2. Place filling in wrappers, fold into triangles, seal edges.
3. Bring chicken stock to boil with ginger and soy sauce.
4. Drop wontons in, cook 4-5 min until they float.
5. Add bok choy in last minute.
6. Ladle into bowls, top with spring onion and white pepper.

title: Chicken Buddha Bowl
summary: Nourishing chicken buddha bowl — balanced and fresh.
instructions:
1. Cook quinoa. Roast cubed sweet potato at 200°C for 25 min.
2. Roast chickpeas with cumin and paprika until crispy.
3. Cook chicken with simple seasoning.
4. Massage kale with olive oil and lemon.
5. Arrange all in a bowl: quinoa, sweet potato, chicken, chickpeas, kale, avocado.
6. Drizzle with tahini-lemon dressing. Nourishing and colorful.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
summary: Fresh chicken caesar salad — light and satisfying.
instructions:
1. Make dressing: blend anchovy, garlic, lemon, dijon, egg yolk, worcestershire, olive oil.
2. Cook chicken until golden and done. Slice.
3. Tear romaine lettuce into pieces.
4. Toast bread cubes with olive oil and garlic for croutons.
5. Toss lettuce with dressing, croutons, shaved parmesan.
6. Top with sliced chicken. Classic — the dressing makes it.

4. Toast bread cubes with olive oil and garlic for croutons.
5. Toss lettuce with dressing, croutons, shaved parmesan.
6. Top with sliced egg. Classic — the dressing makes it.

title: Turkey Caesar Salad
summary: Fresh turkey caesar salad — light and satisfying.
instructions:

3. Tear romaine lettuce into pieces.

title: Thai Chicken Salad
summary: Fresh thai chicken salad — light and satisfying.
instructions:

2. Cook chicken, let cool, then shred or slice.
3. Make dressing: lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chili, garlic.
4. Toss carrot, cabbage, mango, chicken with dressing.
5. Add chopped peanuts, mint, cilantro.
6. Sprinkle sesame seeds. Crunchy, tangy, spicy, fresh — all at once.

instructions:
1. Roast seasonal vegetables at 200°C until caramelized.
2. Cook chicken until golden.
3. Make warm vinaigrette: whisk balsamic, olive oil, honey, mustard.
4. Place greens on plate, top with warm roasted veg and chicken.
5. Crumble goat cheese, sprinkle toasted walnuts.
6. Drizzle warm dressing. The heat wilts greens slightly — perfect.

5. Top with avocado, cheese, sour cream, salsa, crushed chips.
6. Squeeze lime, add cilantro. Tex-Mex salad — all the taco flavors.

title: Classic Pancakes
summary: Delicious classic pancakes — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, salt.
2. Mix egg, milk, melted butter, vanilla separately.
3. Combine wet and dry — mix until just combined (lumps are OK).
4. Heat buttered pan on medium. Pour ¼ cup batter.
5. Flip when bubbles form and edges set.
6. Serve stacked with butter and maple syrup. American breakfast classic.

title: French Toast
summary: Delicious french toast — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Whisk eggs, milk, cinnamon, vanilla, pinch of salt.
2. Use thick slices of brioche or challah.
3. Soak each slice in egg mixture 20 seconds per side.
4. Cook in buttered pan on medium until golden on both sides.
5. The center should be custardy, outside crispy.
6. Top with berries, powdered sugar, maple syrup.

title: Avocado Toast
summary: Delicious avocado toast — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Toast thick sourdough slices until very crunchy.
2. Halve avocado, scoop into bowl. Mash with fork.
3. Add lemon juice, salt, pepper.
4. Spread mashed avocado thickly on toast.
5. Top with a poached or fried egg.
6. Sprinkle chili flakes, drizzle olive oil. Millennial brunch icon.

title: Omelette
summary: Delicious omelette — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Whisk 3 eggs with salt and pepper.
2. Sauté mushroom, bell pepper, onion, spinach briefly.
3. Melt butter in non-stick pan on medium-low.
4. Pour eggs, tilt pan to spread evenly.
5. When almost set, place fillings and cheese on one half.
6. Fold over, slide onto plate. Creamy inside, not browned.

title: Granola Bowl
summary: Delicious granola bowl — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Mix oats, nuts, coconut oil, honey, cinnamon, vanilla, salt.
2. Spread on baking sheet.
3. Bake at 160°C for 25-30 min, stirring every 10 min until golden.
4. Add dried cranberries after cooling.
5. Serve in bowl with thick yogurt.
6. Top with fresh berries and a drizzle of honey. Crunchy and wholesome.

title: Smoothie Bowl
summary: Delicious smoothie bowl — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Freeze banana and berries overnight.
2. Blend frozen fruit with spinach, protein powder, splash of almond milk.
3. Blend thick — thicker than a smoothie.
4. Pour into a bowl.
5. Top with granola, sliced banana, chia seeds, coconut flakes.
6. Drizzle honey. Eat with a spoon — refreshing and filling.

title: Waffles
summary: Delicious waffles — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, salt.
2. Whisk egg yolks, milk, melted butter, vanilla. Combine with dry.
3. Beat egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold into batter gently.
4. Heat waffle iron, grease lightly.
5. Cook until golden and crispy.
6. Top with whipped cream, berries, maple syrup. Crispy outside, fluffy inside.

title: Chilaquiles
summary: Delicious chilaquiles — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Cut tortillas into triangles, fry until crispy.
2. Heat salsa verde in a pan.
3. Add fried tortilla chips to salsa, toss until slightly softened.
4. Fry eggs sunny-side up.
5. Plate chilaquiles, top with fried egg, crumbled cheese, cream.
6. Garnish with avocado and cilantro. Mexican breakfast — crunchy meets saucy.

title: Congee
summary: Delicious congee — great start to the day.
instructions:
1. Cook rice in lots of stock (1:8 ratio) on low heat.
2. Add ginger slices. Stir occasionally.
3. Cook 45-60 min until rice breaks down into thick porridge.
4. Season with soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper.
5. Ladle into bowl.
6. Top with soft-boiled egg, spring onion, fried shallots. Asian comfort food.

title: Chocolate Lava Cake
summary: Irresistible chocolate lava cake — sweet indulgence.
instructions:
1. Melt chocolate and butter together.
2. Whisk eggs and sugar until thick and pale.
3. Fold in melted chocolate, then flour gently.
4. Pour into greased ramekins.
5. Bake at 220°C for exactly 12 min — edges set, center jiggles.
6. Invert onto plate, the molten center flows out. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

title: Panna Cotta
summary: Irresistible panna cotta — sweet indulgence.
instructions:
1. Bloom agar-agar in cold water.
2. Heat cream with sugar and vanilla until just simmering.
3. Add squeezed agar-agar, stir until dissolved.
4. Pour into ramekins or glasses.
5. Chill 4-6 hours until set with a gentle wobble.
6. Top with fresh berries or berry coulis. Italian custard — silky smooth.

title: Mochi
summary: Irresistible mochi — sweet indulgence.
instructions:
1. Mix glutinous rice flour, sugar, water.
2. Microwave 1 min, stir, microwave 1 more min until translucent.
3. Dust surface with cornstarch.
4. Divide dough into pieces.
5. Flatten each, place red bean paste in center, pinch closed.
6. Roll smooth. Chewy Japanese treat — soft and sweet.

title: Crème Caramel
summary: Irresistible crème caramel — sweet indulgence.
instructions:
1. Make caramel: cook sugar until dark amber. Pour into ramekins.
2. Whisk eggs, sugar, warm milk, vanilla.
3. Strain custard into ramekins over caramel.
4. Bake in water bath at 150°C for 45 min.
5. Chill completely — at least 4 hours.
6. Run knife around edge, invert onto plate. Caramel flows over custard.

title: Brownie
summary: Irresistible brownie — sweet indulgence.
instructions:
1. Melt chocolate and butter together. Cool slightly.
2. Whisk eggs and sugar until thick.
3. Fold in chocolate mixture, then flour, cocoa, salt.
4. Add walnuts if desired.
5. Pour into lined pan. Bake at 180°C for 22-25 min.
6. Center should be fudgy, not cakey. Cool before cutting. Best slightly warm.

title: Green Smoothie
summary: Refreshing green smoothie — thirst-quenching.
instructions:
1. Add spinach and almond milk to blender first.
2. Blend until smooth.
3. Add banana, apple, ginger, lemon juice.
4. Blend until creamy.
5. Add chia seeds, pulse briefly.
6. Pour and drink immediately. Nutrient-packed and refreshing.

title: Berry Smoothie
summary: Refreshing berry smoothie — thirst-quenching.
instructions:
1. Wash berries, peel banana.
2. Add all fruit to blender with yogurt.
3. Add honey and ice.
4. Blend until smooth and thick.
5. Pour into glass.
6. Garnish with whole berries. Antioxidant-rich and delicious.

title: Golden Milk
summary: Refreshing golden milk — thirst-quenching.
instructions:
1. Warm milk on medium heat.
2. Add turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, a pinch of black pepper.
3. Whisk until frothy.
4. Add coconut oil and honey.
5. Simmer 5 min on low — don't boil.
6. Strain into a mug. Anti-inflammatory and warming. Haldi doodh.

title: Horchata
summary: Refreshing horchata — thirst-quenching.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and almonds in water for 4 hours.
2. Blend with cinnamon and vanilla until smooth.
3. Strain through cheesecloth — squeeze well.
4. Add sugar, stir until dissolved.
5. Chill completely.
6. Serve over ice. Mexican cinnamon rice drink — sweet and refreshing.

title: Thai Iced Tea
summary: Refreshing thai iced tea — thirst-quenching.
instructions:
1. Brew strong black tea with star anise and cardamom.
2. Add sugar while hot, stir to dissolve.
3. Let cool completely.
4. Fill tall glass with ice.
5. Pour tea over ice, filling ¾ of glass.
6. Slowly pour condensed milk — it sinks and swirls. Stir before drinking. Vibrant orange.

title: Matcha Latte
summary: Refreshing matcha latte — thirst-quenching.
instructions:
1. Sift matcha powder into a bowl — no lumps.
2. Add a splash of hot water (not boiling — 80°C).
3. Whisk vigorously with a chasen (bamboo whisk) until frothy.
4. Heat and froth milk.
5. Pour matcha into a cup, add frothed milk.
6. Drizzle honey if desired. Earthy, creamy, vibrant green.

title: Agua Fresca Watermelon
summary: Refreshing agua fresca watermelon — thirst-quenching.
instructions:
1. Cut watermelon into chunks, remove seeds.
2. Blend with water until smooth.
3. Strain through sieve for smooth texture.
4. Add lime juice, sugar, pinch of salt.
5. Stir well, chill.
6. Serve over ice with mint leaves. Mexican fruit water — pure refreshment.

title: Authentic Litti Chokha
summary: The soul food of Bihar. Roasted wheat balls stuffed with spiced sattu, served with a smoky mash of roasted eggplant, tomatoes, and potatoes (Chokha), drenched in pure desi ghee.
instructions:
Knead wheat flour into dough.
Mix sattu with spices and mustard oil for stuffing.
Stuff dough with sattu and make round balls (Litti).
Roast littis until golden and cracked.
Roast eggplant and tomatoes, peel and mash them with boiled potatoes and raw mustard oil for Chokha.
Dip hot littis in ghee and serve with chokha.

title: Sattu Paratha (Makuni Roti)
summary: Crispy and flaky whole wheat flatbread stuffed with a tangy, spicy roasted black gram flour mixture.
instructions:
Knead soft dough with wheat flour.
Mix sattu with chopped aromatics, mustard oil, lemon juice, and pickle masala.
Stuff dough balls with sattu mixture and roll into flatbreads.
Cook on a hot griddle applying ghee until golden and crisp.
Serve hot with chutney or yogurt.

title: Traditional Dal Pitha
summary: Steamed rice flour dumplings stuffed with a spicy chana dal mixture. A healthy, oil-free delicacy from Bihar.
instructions:
Soak chana dal for 4 hours, then grind coarsely with garlic, ginger, and chilies.
Make a soft dough of rice flour with hot water.
Take small dough portions, flatten into discs, and place the dal stuffing inside.
Fold into semi-circles and seal the edges.
Steam for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.
Serve hot with green chutney.

title: Chana Ghugni
summary: A popular, spicy, and tangy black chickpea curry usually served as a street food or breakfast alongside puffed rice.
instructions:
Soak black chickpeas overnight.
Heat mustard oil, temper with cumin seeds.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomatoes, cook until oil separates.
Add cumin, coriander, chili, garam masala and soaked chickpeas, sauté well.
Add water and pressure cook for 4-5 whistles.
Garnish with chopped onions, green chilies, and lemon juice.

title: Silao Khaja
summary: A famous multi-layered, crispy, and flaky sweet from Silao, Bihar, deep-fried and soaked in sugar syrup.
instructions:
Prepare a stiff dough using flour, ghee, and water.
Roll out very thin large rotis.
Stack the rotis, applying a paste of ghee and flour between each layer.
Roll the stack tightly into a log and cut into 1-inch pieces.
Flatten slightly and deep fry on low heat until golden and crispy layers separate.
Soak briefly in warm sugar syrup and drain.

title: Khasta Thekua
summary: The signature sweet snack of Bihar, especially made during Chhath Puja. Deep-fried, crunchy whole wheat and jaggery cookies.
instructions:
Melt jaggery in a little water and let it cool.
Mix wheat flour with melted ghee, grated coconut, fennel, and cardamom.
Gradually add jaggery syrup to form a stiff, crumbly dough.
Make small round or oval balls and press on a mold for patterns.
Deep fry in ghee on low heat until dark golden and crisp.
Cool completely before storing.

title: Kadhi Badi
summary: A comforting yogurt and gram flour curry with soft fried gram flour fritters (badi). A staple in Bihari households.
instructions:
Make a thick batter of besan, turmeric, and water. Beat well until fluffy.
Drop small portions into hot mustard oil to fry soft badis (fritters).
For kadhi, whisk yogurt, besan, turmeric, and water into a smooth, thin mixture.
Temper mustard oil with cumin, red chilies, and garlic.
Pour the yogurt mixture and stir continuously until it boils.
Simmer, add the fried badis, and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with rice.

title: Champaran Meat (Ahuna Mutton)
summary: Legendary slow-cooked mutton curry sealed in an earthen pot with whole garlic bulbs and mustard oil over a charcoal fire.
instructions:
Heat mustard oil until smoking, then let it cool.
Marinate mutton with sliced onions, ginger-garlic paste, all powdered and whole spices, whole garlic bulbs, and the cooled mustard oil.
Transfer to an earthen pot (handi).
Seal the pot tightly with wheat dough.
Slow cook over charcoal or low heat for 2-2.5 hours, shaking gently every 15 minutes without opening.
Serve hot with rice or rotis.

title: Bihari Malpua
summary: A festive sweet pancake soaked in sugar syrup, often enriched with mashed bananas and served with rabri.
instructions:
Mash ripe banana and mix with flour, semolina, fennel seeds, and milk to form a smooth pouring consistency batter. Rest for 2 hours.
Prepare a one-string consistency sugar syrup flavored with cardamom.
Heat ghee in a flat pan. Pour a ladle of batter to form a pancake.
Fry on low heat until golden on both sides.
Soak hot malpuas in the warm sugar syrup for a minute.
Garnish with nuts and serve warm.

title: Dahi Chura
summary: The traditional Makar Sankranti breakfast of Bihar. Flattened rice mixed with creamy yogurt and jaggery.
instructions:
Wash the flattened rice gently and drain all water.
In a bowl, add the softened flattened rice.
Top generously with thick, fresh yogurt.
Add crushed jaggery or sugar to taste.
Mix in sliced bananas if desired.
Serve immediately.

title: Gaya Tilkut
summary: A famous winter sweet from Gaya, made by pounding roasted sesame seeds and sugar into thin, crispy discs.
instructions:
Dry roast sesame seeds until lightly golden and aromatic. Keep aside.
Boil sugar/jaggery with water to make a very thick, hard-ball stage syrup.
Mix the roasted sesame seeds quickly into the hot syrup.
Pound the mixture continuously with a heavy wooden pestle while it's hot.
Shape them into round discs or cups while pounding.
Let them cool completely to become crisp.

title: Balushahi
summary: A traditional flaky, deep-fried pastry soaked in sugar syrup, known for its melt-in-the-mouth texture.
instructions:
Rub ghee into flour until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add baking soda and yogurt to gently bring the dough together (do not knead).
Make a sticky sugar syrup with cardamom.
Pinch small balls of dough, flatten slightly, and make a deep indentation in the center.
Deep fry on very low heat until golden and crisp (takes 15-20 mins).
Dip the warm balushahis in warm sugar syrup for 5 minutes.
Remove and let the syrup crystallize on top.

title: Bihari Kebabs
summary: Extremely tender, smoky, melt-in-the-mouth meat kebabs marinated with raw papaya, poppy seeds, and mustard oil, cooked over charcoal.
instructions:
Marinate meat strips with raw papaya paste for 2 hours to tenderize.
Mix in roasted onion paste, ginger-garlic paste, poppy seed paste, yogurt, roasted gram flour, kebab masala, and mustard oil.
Marinate for another 4-6 hours or overnight.
Thread the flat meat strips onto skewers.
Grill over a charcoal fire, basting with mustard oil, until charred and cooked.
Serve with sliced onions, lemon wedges, and parathas.

title: Laung Latika
summary: A rich, festive stuffed pastry, folded tightly and pinned with a clove (laung), deep-fried and soaked in sugar syrup.
instructions:
Make a firm dough with flour, water, and ghee.
Roast khoya with chopped nuts, a little sugar, and cardamom for the stuffing.
Roll out small dough circles, place stuffing in the center.
Fold the edges over the stuffing like an envelope and secure the center by piercing a clove (laung) through it.
Deep fry on medium heat until crispy and golden.
Soak in hot sugar syrup for a few minutes and serve.

title: Parwal ki Mithai
summary: A unique sweet from Bihar where pointed gourd (parwal) is boiled in syrup and stuffed with sweetened khoya.
instructions:
Peel parwals, slit them lengthwise, and carefully scrape out all the seeds.
Boil parwals in water with a pinch of baking soda for 3-4 minutes to retain green color, then drain.
Boil them in sugar syrup for 10-15 minutes until soft and glazed. Remove and drain excess syrup.
Roast khoya, mix with powdered sugar, cardamom, and chopped nuts.
Stuff the sweetened parwals generously with the khoya mixture.
Garnish with nuts and silver vark. Chill before serving.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
summary: Classic Indian chicken tikka masala. A creamy, spiced tomato sauce.
instructions:
1. Prepare the chicken by cutting into bite-sized pieces.
2. Heat oil or ghee in a pan and sauté the aromatics.
3. Add the base spices for the tikka masala and cook until fragrant.
4. Add the chicken and cook until well-coated in spices.
5. Simmer on low heat until fully cooked.
6. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with naan or rice.

title: Masala Dosa
summary: Crispy fermented crepe filled with spiced potatoes.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal overnight, then grind to a smooth batter.
2. Ferment the batter for 8-12 hours.
3. Prepare the potato filling by tempering mustard seeds, curry leaves, and onions, then adding mashed potatoes.
4. Spread batter thinly on a hot griddle.
5. Place potato filling in the center and fold. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Idli Sambar
summary: Steamed rice cakes served with lentil and vegetable stew.
instructions:
1. Prepare idli batter and steam in molds for 10-12 minutes.
2. Boil toor dal until soft.
3. Cook vegetables with tamarind extract and sambar powder.
4. Mix dal and vegetable stew, temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
5. Serve hot idlis submerged in sambar.

title: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic basmati rice layered with spiced chicken.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, spices, mint, and fried onions.
2. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices.
3. Layer chicken and rice in a heavy-bottomed pot.
4. Seal the pot with dough and cook on Dum (slow heat) for 40 minutes.
5. Gently mix and serve with raita.

title: Kerala Fish Curry
summary: Spicy and tangy fish curry with coconut milk and kokum.
instructions:
1. Clean and slice the fish.
2. Sauté shallots, ginger, garlic, and curry leaves.
3. Add spice powders and kokum water, bring to a boil.
4. Gently slide in the fish pieces and cook.
5. Finish with coconut milk and simmer. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Upma
summary: Savory semolina porridge tempered with spices.
instructions:
1. Dry roast the semolina until fragrant.
2. Temper mustard seeds, dal, chilies, ginger, and curry leaves in oil.
3. Add water and bring to a rolling boil.
4. Slowly whisk in the roasted semolina to avoid lumps.
5. Cover and cook until water is absorbed. Garnish with coriander.

title: Pani Puri
summary: Crispy hollow puris filled with spicy tangy water.
instructions:
1. Prepare the spicy mint water and sweet tamarind chutney.
2. Mash boiled potatoes and chickpeas with spices.
3. Crack open the puri gently with your thumb.
4. Fill with potato mixture and dip in the spicy water.
5. Eat immediately in one bite.

title: Vada Pav
summary: Spicy potato fritter stuffed in a soft bread bun.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potatoes, mix with tempered mustard seeds, garlic, and chilies.
2. Form into balls, dip in besan batter, and deep fry.
3. Slit the pav and spread dry garlic chutney inside.
4. Place the fried vada inside the pav.
5. Serve hot with fried green chilies.

title: Chole Bhature
summary: Spicy chickpea curry served with fried bread.
instructions:
1. Soak and boil chickpeas until tender.
2. Prepare a thick, spicy gravy with onions, tomatoes, and chole masala.
3. Mix maida, yogurt, and baking powder to form a dough and let it rest.
4. Roll out the dough into discs and deep fry until puffed.
5. Serve hot bhature with chole, onions, and pickle.

title: Pav Bhaji
summary: Spiced vegetable mash served with buttered buns.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash mixed vegetables (potatoes, cauliflower, peas).
2. Sauté onions, tomatoes, and capsicum in butter.
3. Add the mashed vegetables and pav bhaji masala, cook until flavors meld.
4. Toast pav with butter on a griddle.
5. Serve hot bhaji topped with butter, onions, and lemon wedges.

title: Samosa
summary: Crispy pastry stuffed with spiced potatoes and peas.
instructions:
1. Make a stiff dough with maida, oil, and water. Rest for 30 mins.
2. Boil and dice potatoes. Sauté with peas and spices for the filling.
3. Roll dough into circles, cut in half, and form into cones.
4. Fill cones with potato mixture and seal the edges.
5. Deep fry on low-medium heat until golden brown and crispy.

title: Aloo Tikki Chaat
summary: Crispy potato patties topped with yogurt and chutneys.
instructions:
1. Boil and grate potatoes, mix with spices, and shape into patties.
2. Shallow fry the patties until crispy on both sides.
3. Place patties on a plate, lightly crush them.
4. Drizzle generously with whisked yogurt, mint chutney, and tamarind chutney.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala, sev, and chopped coriander.

title: Dhaba Style Masala Dosa
summary: Crispy fermented crepe filled with spiced potatoes.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal overnight, then grind to a smooth batter.
2. Ferment the batter for 8-12 hours.
3. Prepare the potato filling by tempering mustard seeds, curry leaves, and onions, then adding mashed potatoes.
4. Spread batter thinly on a hot griddle.
5. Place potato filling in the center and fold. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Dhaba Style Idli Sambar
summary: Steamed rice cakes served with lentil and vegetable stew.
instructions:
1. Prepare idli batter and steam in molds for 10-12 minutes.
2. Boil toor dal until soft.
3. Cook vegetables with tamarind extract and sambar powder.
4. Mix dal and vegetable stew, temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
5. Serve hot idlis submerged in sambar.

title: Dhaba Style Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic basmati rice layered with spiced chicken.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, spices, mint, and fried onions.
2. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices.
3. Layer chicken and rice in a heavy-bottomed pot.
4. Seal the pot with dough and cook on Dum (slow heat) for 40 minutes.
5. Gently mix and serve with raita.

title: Dhaba Style Kerala Fish Curry
summary: Spicy and tangy fish curry with coconut milk and kokum.
instructions:
1. Clean and slice the fish.
2. Sauté shallots, ginger, garlic, and curry leaves.
3. Add spice powders and kokum water, bring to a boil.
4. Gently slide in the fish pieces and cook.
5. Finish with coconut milk and simmer. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Dhaba Style Upma
summary: Savory semolina porridge tempered with spices.
instructions:
1. Dry roast the semolina until fragrant.
2. Temper mustard seeds, dal, chilies, ginger, and curry leaves in oil.
3. Add water and bring to a rolling boil.
4. Slowly whisk in the roasted semolina to avoid lumps.
5. Cover and cook until water is absorbed. Garnish with coriander.

title: Dhaba Style Pani Puri
summary: Crispy hollow puris filled with spicy tangy water.
instructions:
1. Prepare the spicy mint water and sweet tamarind chutney.
2. Mash boiled potatoes and chickpeas with spices.
3. Crack open the puri gently with your thumb.
4. Fill with potato mixture and dip in the spicy water.
5. Eat immediately in one bite.

title: Dhaba Style Vada Pav
summary: Spicy potato fritter stuffed in a soft bread bun.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potatoes, mix with tempered mustard seeds, garlic, and chilies.
2. Form into balls, dip in besan batter, and deep fry.
3. Slit the pav and spread dry garlic chutney inside.
4. Place the fried vada inside the pav.
5. Serve hot with fried green chilies.

title: Dhaba Style Chole Bhature
summary: Spicy chickpea curry served with fried bread.
instructions:
1. Soak and boil chickpeas until tender.
2. Prepare a thick, spicy gravy with onions, tomatoes, and chole masala.
3. Mix maida, yogurt, and baking powder to form a dough and let it rest.
4. Roll out the dough into discs and deep fry until puffed.
5. Serve hot bhature with chole, onions, and pickle.

title: Dhaba Style Pav Bhaji
summary: Spiced vegetable mash served with buttered buns.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash mixed vegetables (potatoes, cauliflower, peas).
2. Sauté onions, tomatoes, and capsicum in butter.
3. Add the mashed vegetables and pav bhaji masala, cook until flavors meld.
4. Toast pav with butter on a griddle.
5. Serve hot bhaji topped with butter, onions, and lemon wedges.

title: Dhaba Style Samosa
summary: Crispy pastry stuffed with spiced potatoes and peas.
instructions:
1. Make a stiff dough with maida, oil, and water. Rest for 30 mins.
2. Boil and dice potatoes. Sauté with peas and spices for the filling.
3. Roll dough into circles, cut in half, and form into cones.
4. Fill cones with potato mixture and seal the edges.
5. Deep fry on low-medium heat until golden brown and crispy.

title: Dhaba Style Aloo Tikki Chaat
summary: Crispy potato patties topped with yogurt and chutneys.
instructions:
1. Boil and grate potatoes, mix with spices, and shape into patties.
2. Shallow fry the patties until crispy on both sides.
3. Place patties on a plate, lightly crush them.
4. Drizzle generously with whisked yogurt, mint chutney, and tamarind chutney.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala, sev, and chopped coriander.

title: Restaurant Style Masala Dosa
summary: Crispy fermented crepe filled with spiced potatoes.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal overnight, then grind to a smooth batter.
2. Ferment the batter for 8-12 hours.
3. Prepare the potato filling by tempering mustard seeds, curry leaves, and onions, then adding mashed potatoes.
4. Spread batter thinly on a hot griddle.
5. Place potato filling in the center and fold. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Restaurant Style Idli Sambar
summary: Steamed rice cakes served with lentil and vegetable stew.
instructions:
1. Prepare idli batter and steam in molds for 10-12 minutes.
2. Boil toor dal until soft.
3. Cook vegetables with tamarind extract and sambar powder.
4. Mix dal and vegetable stew, temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
5. Serve hot idlis submerged in sambar.

title: Restaurant Style Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic basmati rice layered with spiced chicken.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, spices, mint, and fried onions.
2. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices.
3. Layer chicken and rice in a heavy-bottomed pot.
4. Seal the pot with dough and cook on Dum (slow heat) for 40 minutes.
5. Gently mix and serve with raita.

title: Restaurant Style Kerala Fish Curry
summary: Spicy and tangy fish curry with coconut milk and kokum.
instructions:
1. Clean and slice the fish.
2. Sauté shallots, ginger, garlic, and curry leaves.
3. Add spice powders and kokum water, bring to a boil.
4. Gently slide in the fish pieces and cook.
5. Finish with coconut milk and simmer. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Restaurant Style Upma
summary: Savory semolina porridge tempered with spices.
instructions:
1. Dry roast the semolina until fragrant.
2. Temper mustard seeds, dal, chilies, ginger, and curry leaves in oil.
3. Add water and bring to a rolling boil.
4. Slowly whisk in the roasted semolina to avoid lumps.
5. Cover and cook until water is absorbed. Garnish with coriander.

title: Restaurant Style Pani Puri
summary: Crispy hollow puris filled with spicy tangy water.
instructions:
1. Prepare the spicy mint water and sweet tamarind chutney.
2. Mash boiled potatoes and chickpeas with spices.
3. Crack open the puri gently with your thumb.
4. Fill with potato mixture and dip in the spicy water.
5. Eat immediately in one bite.

title: Restaurant Style Vada Pav
summary: Spicy potato fritter stuffed in a soft bread bun.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potatoes, mix with tempered mustard seeds, garlic, and chilies.
2. Form into balls, dip in besan batter, and deep fry.
3. Slit the pav and spread dry garlic chutney inside.
4. Place the fried vada inside the pav.
5. Serve hot with fried green chilies.

title: Restaurant Style Chole Bhature
summary: Spicy chickpea curry served with fried bread.
instructions:
1. Soak and boil chickpeas until tender.
2. Prepare a thick, spicy gravy with onions, tomatoes, and chole masala.
3. Mix maida, yogurt, and baking powder to form a dough and let it rest.
4. Roll out the dough into discs and deep fry until puffed.
5. Serve hot bhature with chole, onions, and pickle.

title: Restaurant Style Pav Bhaji
summary: Spiced vegetable mash served with buttered buns.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash mixed vegetables (potatoes, cauliflower, peas).
2. Sauté onions, tomatoes, and capsicum in butter.
3. Add the mashed vegetables and pav bhaji masala, cook until flavors meld.
4. Toast pav with butter on a griddle.
5. Serve hot bhaji topped with butter, onions, and lemon wedges.

title: Restaurant Style Samosa
summary: Crispy pastry stuffed with spiced potatoes and peas.
instructions:
1. Make a stiff dough with maida, oil, and water. Rest for 30 mins.
2. Boil and dice potatoes. Sauté with peas and spices for the filling.
3. Roll dough into circles, cut in half, and form into cones.
4. Fill cones with potato mixture and seal the edges.
5. Deep fry on low-medium heat until golden brown and crispy.

title: Restaurant Style Aloo Tikki Chaat
summary: Crispy potato patties topped with yogurt and chutneys.
instructions:
1. Boil and grate potatoes, mix with spices, and shape into patties.
2. Shallow fry the patties until crispy on both sides.
3. Place patties on a plate, lightly crush them.
4. Drizzle generously with whisked yogurt, mint chutney, and tamarind chutney.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala, sev, and chopped coriander.

title: Homestyle Chicken Tikka Masala
summary: Classic Indian chicken tikka masala. A creamy, spiced tomato sauce.
instructions:
1. Prepare the chicken by cutting into bite-sized pieces.
2. Heat oil or ghee in a pan and sauté the aromatics.
3. Add the base spices for the tikka masala and cook until fragrant.
4. Add the chicken and cook until well-coated in spices.
5. Simmer on low heat until fully cooked.
6. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot with naan or rice.

title: Homestyle Masala Dosa
summary: Crispy fermented crepe filled with spiced potatoes.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal overnight, then grind to a smooth batter.
2. Ferment the batter for 8-12 hours.
3. Prepare the potato filling by tempering mustard seeds, curry leaves, and onions, then adding mashed potatoes.
4. Spread batter thinly on a hot griddle.
5. Place potato filling in the center and fold. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Homestyle Idli Sambar
summary: Steamed rice cakes served with lentil and vegetable stew.
instructions:
1. Prepare idli batter and steam in molds for 10-12 minutes.
2. Boil toor dal until soft.
3. Cook vegetables with tamarind extract and sambar powder.
4. Mix dal and vegetable stew, temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
5. Serve hot idlis submerged in sambar.

title: Homestyle Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic basmati rice layered with spiced chicken.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, spices, mint, and fried onions.
2. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices.
3. Layer chicken and rice in a heavy-bottomed pot.
4. Seal the pot with dough and cook on Dum (slow heat) for 40 minutes.
5. Gently mix and serve with raita.

title: Homestyle Kerala Fish Curry
summary: Spicy and tangy fish curry with coconut milk and kokum.
instructions:
1. Clean and slice the fish.
2. Sauté shallots, ginger, garlic, and curry leaves.
3. Add spice powders and kokum water, bring to a boil.
4. Gently slide in the fish pieces and cook.
5. Finish with coconut milk and simmer. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Homestyle Upma
summary: Savory semolina porridge tempered with spices.
instructions:
1. Dry roast the semolina until fragrant.
2. Temper mustard seeds, dal, chilies, ginger, and curry leaves in oil.
3. Add water and bring to a rolling boil.
4. Slowly whisk in the roasted semolina to avoid lumps.
5. Cover and cook until water is absorbed. Garnish with coriander.

title: Homestyle Pani Puri
summary: Crispy hollow puris filled with spicy tangy water.
instructions:
1. Prepare the spicy mint water and sweet tamarind chutney.
2. Mash boiled potatoes and chickpeas with spices.
3. Crack open the puri gently with your thumb.
4. Fill with potato mixture and dip in the spicy water.
5. Eat immediately in one bite.

title: Homestyle Vada Pav
summary: Spicy potato fritter stuffed in a soft bread bun.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potatoes, mix with tempered mustard seeds, garlic, and chilies.
2. Form into balls, dip in besan batter, and deep fry.
3. Slit the pav and spread dry garlic chutney inside.
4. Place the fried vada inside the pav.
5. Serve hot with fried green chilies.

title: Homestyle Chole Bhature
summary: Spicy chickpea curry served with fried bread.
instructions:
1. Soak and boil chickpeas until tender.
2. Prepare a thick, spicy gravy with onions, tomatoes, and chole masala.
3. Mix maida, yogurt, and baking powder to form a dough and let it rest.
4. Roll out the dough into discs and deep fry until puffed.
5. Serve hot bhature with chole, onions, and pickle.

title: Homestyle Pav Bhaji
summary: Spiced vegetable mash served with buttered buns.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash mixed vegetables (potatoes, cauliflower, peas).
2. Sauté onions, tomatoes, and capsicum in butter.
3. Add the mashed vegetables and pav bhaji masala, cook until flavors meld.
4. Toast pav with butter on a griddle.
5. Serve hot bhaji topped with butter, onions, and lemon wedges.

title: Homestyle Samosa
summary: Crispy pastry stuffed with spiced potatoes and peas.
instructions:
1. Make a stiff dough with maida, oil, and water. Rest for 30 mins.
2. Boil and dice potatoes. Sauté with peas and spices for the filling.
3. Roll dough into circles, cut in half, and form into cones.
4. Fill cones with potato mixture and seal the edges.
5. Deep fry on low-medium heat until golden brown and crispy.

title: Homestyle Aloo Tikki Chaat
summary: Crispy potato patties topped with yogurt and chutneys.
instructions:
1. Boil and grate potatoes, mix with spices, and shape into patties.
2. Shallow fry the patties until crispy on both sides.
3. Place patties on a plate, lightly crush them.
4. Drizzle generously with whisked yogurt, mint chutney, and tamarind chutney.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala, sev, and chopped coriander.

4. Add the chicken and cook until well-coated in spices.

title: Spicy Masala Dosa
summary: Crispy fermented crepe filled with spiced potatoes.
instructions:
1. Soak rice and dal overnight, then grind to a smooth batter.
2. Ferment the batter for 8-12 hours.
3. Prepare the potato filling by tempering mustard seeds, curry leaves, and onions, then adding mashed potatoes.
4. Spread batter thinly on a hot griddle.
5. Place potato filling in the center and fold. Serve with sambar and chutney.

title: Spicy Idli Sambar
summary: Steamed rice cakes served with lentil and vegetable stew.
instructions:
1. Prepare idli batter and steam in molds for 10-12 minutes.
2. Boil toor dal until soft.
3. Cook vegetables with tamarind extract and sambar powder.
4. Mix dal and vegetable stew, temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
5. Serve hot idlis submerged in sambar.

title: Spicy Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
summary: Aromatic basmati rice layered with spiced chicken.
instructions:
1. Marinate chicken in yogurt, spices, mint, and fried onions.
2. Parboil basmati rice with whole spices.
3. Layer chicken and rice in a heavy-bottomed pot.
4. Seal the pot with dough and cook on Dum (slow heat) for 40 minutes.
5. Gently mix and serve with raita.

title: Spicy Kerala Fish Curry
summary: Spicy and tangy fish curry with coconut milk and kokum.
instructions:
1. Clean and slice the fish.
2. Sauté shallots, ginger, garlic, and curry leaves.
3. Add spice powders and kokum water, bring to a boil.
4. Gently slide in the fish pieces and cook.
5. Finish with coconut milk and simmer. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Spicy Upma
summary: Savory semolina porridge tempered with spices.
instructions:
1. Dry roast the semolina until fragrant.
2. Temper mustard seeds, dal, chilies, ginger, and curry leaves in oil.
3. Add water and bring to a rolling boil.
4. Slowly whisk in the roasted semolina to avoid lumps.
5. Cover and cook until water is absorbed. Garnish with coriander.

title: Spicy Pani Puri
summary: Crispy hollow puris filled with spicy tangy water.
instructions:
1. Prepare the spicy mint water and sweet tamarind chutney.
2. Mash boiled potatoes and chickpeas with spices.
3. Crack open the puri gently with your thumb.
4. Fill with potato mixture and dip in the spicy water.
5. Eat immediately in one bite.

title: Spicy Vada Pav
summary: Spicy potato fritter stuffed in a soft bread bun.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash potatoes, mix with tempered mustard seeds, garlic, and chilies.
2. Form into balls, dip in besan batter, and deep fry.
3. Slit the pav and spread dry garlic chutney inside.
4. Place the fried vada inside the pav.
5. Serve hot with fried green chilies.

title: Spicy Chole Bhature
summary: Spicy chickpea curry served with fried bread.
instructions:
1. Soak and boil chickpeas until tender.
2. Prepare a thick, spicy gravy with onions, tomatoes, and chole masala.
3. Mix maida, yogurt, and baking powder to form a dough and let it rest.
4. Roll out the dough into discs and deep fry until puffed.
5. Serve hot bhature with chole, onions, and pickle.

title: Spicy Pav Bhaji
summary: Spiced vegetable mash served with buttered buns.
instructions:
1. Boil and mash mixed vegetables (potatoes, cauliflower, peas).
2. Sauté onions, tomatoes, and capsicum in butter.
3. Add the mashed vegetables and pav bhaji masala, cook until flavors meld.
4. Toast pav with butter on a griddle.
5. Serve hot bhaji topped with butter, onions, and lemon wedges.

title: Spicy Samosa
summary: Crispy pastry stuffed with spiced potatoes and peas.
instructions:
1. Make a stiff dough with maida, oil, and water. Rest for 30 mins.
2. Boil and dice potatoes. Sauté with peas and spices for the filling.
3. Roll dough into circles, cut in half, and form into cones.
4. Fill cones with potato mixture and seal the edges.
5. Deep fry on low-medium heat until golden brown and crispy.

title: Spicy Aloo Tikki Chaat
summary: Crispy potato patties topped with yogurt and chutneys.
instructions:
1. Boil and grate potatoes, mix with spices, and shape into patties.
2. Shallow fry the patties until crispy on both sides.
3. Place patties on a plate, lightly crush them.
4. Drizzle generously with whisked yogurt, mint chutney, and tamarind chutney.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala, sev, and chopped coriander.
